वेदानां सामवेदस्त्वं गायत्री छन्दसामसि ॥
1.11.m: Among the Ādityas you are Upendra; and among the Vasus you are Fire; / among the Vedas you are the Sāmaveda; among meters you are the Gāyatrī.

1.11.s:
adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ gatīnāṃ param gatiḥ /
māyā tvaṃ sarvaśaktīnāṃ kālaḥ kalayatāmasi //
1.11.d:
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां गतीनां परम् गतिः ।
माया त्वं सर्वशक्तीनां कालः कलयतामसि ॥
1.11.m: Among branches of knowledge [you are] the knowledge of the supreme Self; among destinations, the highest destination; / among all powers you are illusory creative power; among reckoners you are Time.

1.11.s:
oṅkāraḥ sarvaguhyānāṃ varṇānāṃ ca dvijāttamaḥ /
āśramāṇāṃ ca gārhasthyamīśvarāṇāṃ maheśvaraḥ //
1.11.d:
ओङ्कारः सर्वगुह्यानां वर्णानां च द्विजात्तमः ।
आश्रमाणां च गार्हस्थ्यमीश्वराणां महेश्वरः ॥
1.11.m: Among all secrets [you are] the syllable Om; among castes, the best of the twice-born; / among stages of life, the householder's life; among lords, the Great Lord.

1.11.s:
puṃsāṃ tvamekaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvabhūtahṛdi sthitaḥ /
sarvopaniṣadāṃ devi guhyopaniṣaducyate //
1.11.d:
पुंसां त्वमेकः पुरुषः सर्वभूतहृदि स्थितः ।
सर्वोपनिषदां देवि गुह्योपनिषदुच्यते ॥
1.11.m: Among spirits you are the one Spirit abiding in the heart of all beings; / among all Upaniṣads, O goddess, you are called the Secret Upaniṣad.

1.11.s:
īśānaścāsi kalpānāṃ yugānāṃ kṛtameva ca /
ādityaḥ sarvamārgāṇāṃ vācāṃ devi sarasvatī //
1.11.d:
ईशानश्चासि कल्पानां युगानां कृतमेव च ।
आदित्यः सर्वमार्गाणां वाचां देवि सरस्वती ॥
1.11.m: You are the Īśāna of cosmic eons, and the Kṛta of the cosmic ages; / among all paths, the Sun; among speech, O goddess, Sarasvatī.

1.11.s:
tvaṃ lakṣmīścārurūpāṇāṃ viṣṇurmāyāvināmasi /
arundhatī satīnāṃ tvaṃ suparṇaḥ patatāmasi //
1.11.d:
त्वं लक्ष्मीश्चारुरूपाणां विष्णुर्मायाविनामसि ।
अरुन्धती सतीनां त्वं सुपर्णः पततामसि ॥
1.11.m: You are Lakṣmī among beautiful forms; among wielders of illusory power you are Viṣṇu; / among faithful wives you are Arundhatī; among winged creatures you are Suparṇa.

1.11.s:
sūktānāṃ pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ jyeṣṭhasāma ca sāmasu /
sāvitrī cāsi japyānāṃ yajuṣāṃ śatarudriyam //
1.11.d:
सूक्तानां पौरुषं सूक्तं ज्येष्ठसाम च सामसु ।
सावित्री चासि जप्यानां यजुषां शतरुद्रियम् ॥
1.11.m: Among hymns [you are] the Puruṣasūkta, and the Jyeṣṭhasāman among Sāman chants; / among chants to be repeated you are the Sāvitrī, and the Śatarudriya among Yajurvedic texts.

1.11.s:
parvatānāṃ mahāmerurananto bhogināmasi /
sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ paraṃ brahma tvanmayaṃ sarvameva hi //
1.11.d:
पर्वतानां महामेरुरनन्तो भोगिनामसि ।
सर्वेषां त्वं परं ब्रह्म त्वन्मयं सर्वमेव हि ॥
1.11.m: Among mountains you are Mount Meru; among serpent beings you are Ananta; / of all things you are the supreme Brahman; indeed everything is composed of you.

1.11.s:
rūpaṃ tavośeṣakalāvihīna-
magocaraṃ nirmalamekarūpam /
anādimadhyāntamanantāmādyaṃ
namāmi satyaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt //
1.11.d:
रूपं तवोशेषकलाविहीन-
मगोचरं निर्मलमेकरूपम् ।
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तामाद्यं
नमामि सत्यं तमसः परस्तात् ॥
1.11.m: That form of yours devoid of all division, / beyond sense perception, spotless, uniform, / without beginning, middle, or end, endless, primeval, / true, beyond darkness: to that I bow.

1.11.s:
yadeva paśyanti jagatprasūtiṃ
vedāntavijñānaviniścitārthāḥ /
ānandamātraṃ praṇavābhidhānaṃ
tadeva rūpaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.11.d:
यदेव पश्यन्ति जगत्प्रसूतिं
वेदान्तविज्ञानविनिश्चितार्थाः ।
आनन्दमात्रं प्रणवाभिधानं
तदेव रूपं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.11.m: That very form which those who have ascertained the true meaning of the Vedānta / behold as the source of the world, pure bliss, named Praṇava: / to that very form I fly for refuge.

1.11.s:
aśeṣabhūtāntarasanniviṣṭaṃ
pradhānapuṃyogaviyogahetum /
tejomayaṃ janmavināśahīnaṃ
prāṇābhidhānaṃ praṇato 'smi rūpam //
1.11.d:
अशेषभूतान्तरसन्निविष्टं
प्रधानपुंयोगवियोगहेतुम् ।
तेजोमयं जन्मविनाशहीनं
प्राणाभिधानं प्रणतो ऽस्मि रूपम् ॥
1.11.m: Entered into the interior of all beings, / the cause of the union and disjunction of primordial matter and the spirit, / luminous, free from birth and destruction, / named the Breath of Life: to that form I bow.”

1.11.s:
ādyantahīnaṃ jagadātmabhūtaṃ
vibhinnasaṃsthaṃ prakṛteḥ parastāt /
kūṭasthamavyaktavapustavaiva
namāmi rūpaṃ puruṣābhidhānam //
1.11.d:
आद्यन्तहीनं जगदात्मभूतं
विभिन्नसंस्थं प्रकृतेः परस्तात् ।
कूटस्थमव्यक्तवपुस्तवैव
नमामि रूपं पुरुषाभिधानम् ॥
1.11.m: Devoid of beginning and end, being the soul of the universe, / standing diverse, beyond primordial matter, / immovable, whose body is unmanifest—to this very form of yours / called Puruṣa, I bow.

1.11.s:
sarvāśrayaṃ sarvajagadvidhānaṃ
sarvatragaṃ janmavināśahīnam /
sūkṣmaṃ vicitraṃ triguṇaṃ pradhānaṃ
nato 'smi te rūpamaluptabhedam //
1.11.d:
सर्वाश्रयं सर्वजगद्विधानं
सर्वत्रगं जन्मविनाशहीनम् ।
सूक्ष्मं विचित्रं त्रिगुणं प्रधानं
नतो ऽस्मि ते रूपमलुप्तभेदम् ॥
1.11.m: The refuge of all, the arranger of the whole universe, / all-pervading, devoid of birth and destruction, / subtle, manifold, composed of the three qualities, the primary matter— / I bow to this form of yours whose distinctions are never lost.

1.11.s:
ādyaṃ mahat te puruṣātmarūpaṃ
prakṛtyavasthaṃ triguṇātmabījam /
aiśvaryavijñānavirāgadharmaiḥ
samanvitaṃ devi nato 'smi rūpam //
1.11.d:
आद्यं महत् ते पुरुषात्मरूपं
प्रकृत्यवस्थं त्रिगुणात्मबीजम् ।
ऐश्वर्यविज्ञानविरागधर्मैः
समन्वितं देवि नतो ऽस्मि रूपम् ॥
1.11.m: The first, the Great, your form that is the soul of Puruṣa, / situated in primordial matter, the seed composed of the three qualities, / endowed with sovereignty, knowledge, dispassion, and virtue— / O goddess, I bow to your form.

1.11.s:
dvisaptalokātmakamambusaṃsthaṃ
vicitrabhedaṃ puruṣaikanātham /
anantabhūtairadhivāsitaṃ te
nato 'smi rūpaṃ jagadaṇḍasaṃjñam //
1.11.d:
द्विसप्तलोकात्मकमम्बुसंस्थं
विचित्रभेदं पुरुषैकनाथम् ।
अनन्तभूतैरधिवासितं ते
नतो ऽस्मि रूपं जगदण्डसंज्ञम् ॥
1.11.m: Composed of the twice-seven worlds, residing in the waters, / possessing manifold distinctions, having the one Puruṣa as lord, / inhabited by endless living beings— / I bow to this form of yours known as the cosmic egg.

1.11.s:
aśeṣavedātmakamekamādyaṃ
svatejasā pūritalokabhedam /
trikālahetuṃ rapameṣṭhisaṃjñaṃ
namāmi rūpaṃ ravimaṇḍalastham //
1.11.d:
अशेषवेदात्मकमेकमाद्यं
स्वतेजसा पूरितलोकभेदम् ।
त्रिकालहेतुं रपमेष्ठिसंज्ञं
नमामि रूपं रविमण्डलस्थम् ॥
1.11.m: Consisting of all the Vedas, single, primary, / filling the distinct worlds with its own radiance, / the cause of the three divisions of time, called the Supreme Lord— / I bow to the form residing in the solar orb.

1.11.s:
sahastramūrdhānamanantaśaktiṃ
sahastrabāhuṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam /
śayānamantaḥ salile tathaiva
nārāyaṇākhyaṃ praṇato 'smi rūpam //
1.11.d:
सहस्त्रमूर्धानमनन्तशक्तिं
सहस्त्रबाहुं पुरुषं पुराणम् ।
शयानमन्तः सलिले तथैव
नारायणाख्यं प्रणतो ऽस्मि रूपम् ॥
1.11.m: Having a thousand heads, infinite power, / a thousand arms, the ancient Puruṣa, / sleeping likewise within the waters— / I bow to the form named Nārāyaṇa.

1.11.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ tridaśābhivandyaṃ
yugāntakālānalakalparūpam /
aśeṣabhūtāṇḍavināśahetuṃ
namāmi rūpaṃ tava kālasaṃjñam //
1.11.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालं त्रिदशाभिवन्द्यं
युगान्तकालानलकल्परूपम् ।
अशेषभूताण्डविनाशहेतुं
नमामि रूपं तव कालसंज्ञम् ॥
1.11.m: Fierce with fangs, worthy of adoration by the gods, / having a form resembling the fire of time at the end of the cosmic age, / the cause of the destruction of all realms of living beings— / I bow to this form of yours known as Time.

1.11.s:
phaṇāsahastreṇa virājamānaṃ
bhogīndramukhyairabhipūjyamānam /
janārdanārūḍhatanuṃ prasuptaṃ
nato 'smi rūpaṃ tava śeṣasaṃjñam //
1.11.d:
फणासहस्त्रेण विराजमानं
भोगीन्द्रमुख्यैरभिपूज्यमानम् ।
जनार्दनारूढतनुं प्रसुप्तं
नतो ऽस्मि रूपं तव शेषसंज्ञम् ॥
1.11.m: Shining with a thousand hoods, / worshipped by the foremost lords of serpents, / upon whose body Janārdana rests sleeping— / I bow to this form of yours known as Śeṣa.

1.11.s:
avyāhataiśvaryamayugmanetraṃ
brahmāmṛtānandarasajñamekam /
yugāntaśeṣaṃ divi nṛtyamānaṃ
nato 'smi rūpaṃ tava rudrasaṃjñam //
1.11.d:
अव्याहतैश्वर्यमयुग्मनेत्रं
ब्रह्मामृतानन्दरसज्ञमेकम् ।
युगान्तशेषं दिवि नृत्यमानं
नतो ऽस्मि रूपं तव रुद्रसंज्ञम् ॥
1.11.m: With unimpeded sovereignty, odd-eyed, / the sole knower of the nectar of bliss that is Brahman, / remaining at the end of the cosmic age, dancing in heaven— / I bow to this form of yours known as Rudra.

1.11.s:
prahīṇaśokaṃ vimalaṃ pavitraṃ
surāsurairarcitāpādapadmam /
sukomalaṃ devi viśālaśumraṃ
namāmi te rūpamidaṃ namāsi //
1.11.d:
प्रहीणशोकं विमलं पवित्रं
सुरासुरैरर्चितापादपद्मम् ।
सुकोमलं देवि विशालशुम्रं
नमामि ते रूपमिदं नमासि ॥
1.11.m: Free from sorrow, stainless, pure, / whose lotus-feet are worshipped by gods and anti-gods, / exceedingly tender, O goddess, expansive and white— / I bow to this form of yours, I bow.

1.11.s:
oṃ namaste mahādevi namaste parameśvari /
namo bhagavatīśāni śivāyai te namo namaḥ //
1.11.d:
ओं नमस्ते महादेवि नमस्ते परमेश्वरि ।
नमो भगवतीशानि शिवायै ते नमो नमः ॥
1.11.m: Om! Praise to you, O Great Goddess! Praise to you, O Supreme Mistress! / Praise, O sovereign lady, O Śivā, praise and praise to you!

1.11.s:
tvanmayo 'haṃ tvadādhārastvameva ca gatirmama /
tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ yāsye prasīda parameśvari //
1.11.d:
त्वन्मयो ऽहं त्वदाधारस्त्वमेव च गतिर्मम ।
त्वामेव शरणं यास्ये प्रसीद परमेश्वरि ॥
1.11.m: I am composed of you, supported by you, and you alone are my refuge. / To you alone I resort for protection; be gracious, O Supreme Mistress!

1.11.s:
mayā nāsti samo loke devo vādānavo 'pi vā /
jaganmātaiva matputrī saṃbhūtā tapasā yataḥ //
1.11.d:
मया नास्ति समो लोके देवो वादानवो ऽपि वा ।
जगन्मातैव मत्पुत्री संभूता तपसा यतः ॥
1.11.m: There is no one equal to me in the world, whether god or Dānava, / since the Mother of the Universe herself was born as my daughter through austerities.

1.11.s:
eṣā tavāmbikā devi kilābhūta pitṛkanyakā /
menāśeṣajaganmāturaho vuṇyasya gauravam //
1.11.d:
एषा तवाम्बिका देवि किलाभूत पितृकन्यका ।
मेनाशेषजगन्मातुरहो वुण्यस्य गौरवम् ॥
1.11.m: This Ambikā of yours, O goddess, indeed became the daughter of the Pitṛs; / Menā is the mother of the entire universe—oh, the greatness of her merit!

1.11.s:
pāhi māmamareśāni menayā saha sarvadā /
namāmi tava pādābjaṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ śivām //
1.11.d:
पाहि माममरेशानि मेनया सह सर्वदा ।
नमामि तव पादाब्जं व्रजामि शरणं शिवाम् ॥
1.11.m: Protect me always, O sovereign lady of the immortals, together with Menā! / I bow to your lotus-feet; I take refuge in Śivā.

1.11.s:
aho me sumahad bhāgyaṃ mahādevīsamāgamāt /
ājñāpaya mahādevi kiṃ kariṣyāmi śaṅkari //
1.11.d:
अहो मे सुमहद् भाग्यं महादेवीसमागमात् ।
आज्ञापय महादेवि किं करिष्यामि शङ्करि ॥
1.11.m: Oh, how great is my good fortune because of this union with the Great Goddess! / Command me, O Great Goddess! What shall I do, O Śaṅkarī?

1.11.s:
etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ tadā himagirīśvaraḥ /
saṃprekṣaṇamāṇo girijāṃ prāñjaliḥ pārśvato 'bhavat //
1.11.d:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं तदा हिमगिरीश्वरः ।
संप्रेक्षणमाणो गिरिजां प्राञ्जलिः पार्श्वतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.11.m: Having spoken these words then, the lord of the snowy mountains, / gazing upon Girijā with folded hands, stood beside her.

1.11.s:
atha sā tasya vacanaṃ niśamya jagato 'raṇiḥ /
sasmitaṃ prāha pitaraṃ smṛtvā paśupatiṃ patim //
1.11.d:
अथ सा तस्य वचनं निशम्य जगतो ऽरणिः ।
सस्मितं प्राह पितरं स्मृत्वा पशुपतिं पतिम् ॥
1.11.m: Then, hearing his speech, she, the kindling-stick of the universe, / smiling, spoke to her father, remembering her husband, the Lord of Beasts.

1.11.s:
devyuvāca
śṛṇuṣva caitat paramaṃ guhyamīśvaragocaram /
upadeśaṃ giriśreṣṭha sevitaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ //
1.11.d:
देव्युवाच
शृणुष्व चैतत् परमं गुह्यमीश्वरगोचरम् ।
उपदेशं गिरिश्रेष्ठ सेवितं ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥
1.11.m: The goddess said: / Listen to this highest, secret instruction concerning the Supreme Lord, / O best of mountains, practiced by the teachers of Brahman.

1.11.s:
yanme sākṣāt paraṃ rūpamaiśvaraṃ dṛṣṭamadbhutam /
sarvaśaktisamāyuktamanantaṃ prerakaṃ param //
1.11.d:
यन्मे साक्षात् परं रूपमैश्वरं दृष्टमद्भुतम् ।
सर्वशक्तिसमायुक्तमनन्तं प्रेरकं परम् ॥
1.11.m: That highest sovereign form of mine directly seen by you, wondrous, / endowed with all powers, infinite, the supreme impeller—

1.11.s:
śāntaḥ samāhitamanā dambhāhaṅkāravarjitaḥ /
tanniṣṭhastatparo bhūtvā tadeva śaraṇaṃ vraja //
1.11.d:
शान्तः समाहितमना दम्भाहङ्कारवर्जितः ।
तन्निष्ठस्तत्परो भूत्वा तदेव शरणं व्रज ॥
1.11.m: Being tranquil, with a focused mind, free from deceit and egotism, / devoted to it, intent upon it, take refuge in that alone.

1.11.s:
bhaktyā tvananyayā tāta padbhāvaṃ paramāśritaḥ /
sarvayajñatapodānaistadevārcaya sarvadā //
1.11.d:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया तात पद्भावं परमाश्रितः ।
सर्वयज्ञतपोदानैस्तदेवार्चय सर्वदा ॥
1.11.m: With unswerving devotion, dear father, fully taking refuge in my nature, / worship that alone at all times through all sacrifices, austerities, and gifts.

1.11.s:
tadeva manasā paśya tad dhyāyasva japasva ca /
mamopadeśāt saṃsāraṃ nāśayāmi tavānagha //
1.11.d:
तदेव मनसा पश्य तद् ध्यायस्व जपस्व च ।
ममोपदेशात् संसारं नाशयामि तवानघ ॥
1.11.m: Behold that alone with the mind; meditate on that and recite it. / Through my instruction, O sinless one, I shall destroy your worldly existence.

1.11.s:
ahaṃ vai matparān bhaktānaiśvaraṃ yogamāsthitān /
saṃsārasāgarādasmāduddharāmyacireṇa tu //
1.11.d:
अहं वै मत्परान् भक्तानैश्वरं योगमास्थितान् ।
संसारसागरादस्मादुद्धराम्यचिरेण तु ॥
1.11.m: I myself shall swiftly lift out of this ocean of worldly existence / those devotees devoted to me who have undertaken sovereign yoga.

1.11.s:
dhyānena karmayogena bhaktyā jñānena caiva hi /
prāpyāhaṃ te giriśreṣṭha nānyathā karmakoṭibhiḥ //
1.11.d:
ध्यानेन कर्मयोगेन भक्त्या ज्ञानेन चैव हि ।
प्राप्याहं ते गिरिश्रेष्ठ नान्यथा कर्मकोटिभिः ॥
1.11.m: Through meditation, the yoga of action, devotion, and knowledge indeed / am I to be attained by you, O best of mountains, not otherwise through crores of actions.

1.11.s:
śrutismṛtyuditaṃ samyak karma varṇāśramātmakam /
adhyātmajñānasahitaṃ muktaye satataṃ kuru //
1.11.d:
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितं सम्यक् कर्म वर्णाश्रमात्मकम् ।
अध्यात्मज्ञानसहितं मुक्तये सततं कुरु ॥
1.11.m: Action enjoined by the Śruti and Smṛti, consisting of duties of class and life-stage, / combined with knowledge of the supreme Self—perform this constantly for liberation.

1.11.s:
dharmāt saṃjāyate bhaktirbhaktyā saṃprāpyate param /
śrutismṛtibhyāmudito dharmo yajñādiko mataḥ //
1.11.d:
धर्मात् संजायते भक्तिर्भक्त्या संप्राप्यते परम् ।
श्रुतिस्मृतिभ्यामुदितो धर्मो यज्ञादिको मतः ॥
1.11.m: From duty devotion is born; through devotion the Supreme is attained. / Duty enjoined by the Śruti and Smṛti is held to be sacrifice and the like.

1.11.s:
nānyato jāyate dharmo vedād dharmo hi nirbabhau /
tasmānmumukṣurdharmārtho madrūpaṃ vedamāśrayet //
1.11.d:
नान्यतो जायते धर्मो वेदाद् धर्मो हि निर्बभौ ।
तस्मान्मुमुक्षुर्धर्मार्थो मद्रूपं वेदमाश्रयेत् ॥
1.11.m: Duty is not born from anything else; for duty shone forth from the Veda. / Therefore the seeker of liberation who desires duty should take refuge in my form, the Veda.

1.11.s:
mamaivaiṣā parā śaktirvedasaṃjñā purātanī /
ṛgyajuḥ sāmarūpeṇa sargādau saṃpravartate //
1.11.d:
ममैवैषा परा शक्तिर्वेदसंज्ञा पुरातनी ।
ऋग्यजुः सामरूपेण सर्गादौ संप्रवर्तते ॥
1.11.m: This is my supreme ancient power known as the Veda; / in the form of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma, it proceeds at the beginning of primary creation.

1.11.s:
teṣāmeva ca guptyarthaṃ vedānāṃ bhagavānajaḥ /
brāhmaṇādīn sasarjātha sve sve karmaṇyayojayat //
1.11.d:
तेषामेव च गुप्त्यर्थं वेदानां भगवानजः ।
ब्राह्मणादीन् ससर्जाथ स्वे स्वे कर्मण्ययोजयत् ॥
1.11.m: And for the protection of those very Vedas, the unborn Lord / then created the brāhmaṇas and others and appointed them each to their proper action.

1.11.s:
ye na kurvanti tad dharmaṃ tadarthaṃ brahmanirmitam /
teṣāmadhastād narakāṃstāmistrādīnakalpayat //
1.11.d:
ये न कुर्वन्ति तद् धर्मं तदर्थं ब्रह्मनिर्मितम् ।
तेषामधस्ताद् नरकांस्तामिस्त्रादीनकल्पयत् ॥
1.11.m: For those who do not perform that duty fashioned by Brahman for that purpose, / he created hells below, beginning with Tāmisra.

1.11.s:
na ca vedād ṛte kiñcicchāstradharmābhidhāyakam /
yo 'nyatraramateso 'saunasaṃbhāṣyo dvijātibhiḥ //
1.11.d:
न च वेदाद् ऋते किञ्चिच्छास्त्रधर्माभिधायकम् ।
यो ऽन्यत्ररमतेसो ऽसौनसंभाष्यो द्विजातिभिः ॥
1.11.m: And other than the Veda, there is no scripture proclaiming duty; / he who delights elsewhere is not to be spoken to by the twice-born.

1.11.s:
yāni śāstrāṇi dṛśyante loke 'smin vividhānitu /
śrutismṛtiviruddhāni niṣṭhā teṣāṃ hi tāmasī //
1.11.d:
यानि शास्त्राणि दृश्यन्ते लोके ऽस्मिन् विविधानितु ।
श्रुतिस्मृतिविरुद्धानि निष्ठा तेषां हि तामसी ॥
1.11.m: Those various scriptures that are seen in this world, however, / opposed to the Śruti and Smṛti, their basis is indeed rooted in darkness.

1.11.s:
kāpālaṃ pañcarātraṃ ca yāmalaṃ vāmamārhatam /
evaṃvidhāni cānyāni mohanārthāni tāni tu //
1.11.d:
कापालं पञ्चरात्रं च यामलं वाममार्हतम् ।
एवंविधानि चान्यानि मोहनार्थानि तानि तु ॥
1.11.m: Kāpāla, Pañcarātra, Yāmala, Vāma, and Arhata, / and others of this kind—they exist only for the purpose of delusion.

1.11.s:
ye kuśāstrābhiyogena mohayantīha mānavān /
mayā sṛṣṭāni śāstrāṇi mohāyaiṣāṃ bhavāntare //
1.11.d:
ये कुशास्त्राभियोगेन मोहयन्तीह मानवान् ।
मया सृष्टानि शास्त्राणि मोहायैषां भवान्तरे ॥
1.11.m: Those who delude humans here through attachment to false scriptures— / scriptures were created by me for their delusion in another life.

1.11.s:
vedārthavittamaiḥ kāryaṃ yat smṛtaṃ karma vaidikam /
tat prayatnena kurvanti matpriyāste hi ye narāḥ //
1.11.d:
वेदार्थवित्तमैः कार्यं यत् स्मृतं कर्म वैदिकम् ।
तत् प्रयत्नेन कुर्वन्ति मत्प्रियास्ते हि ये नराः ॥
1.11.m: The Vedic action which is remembered as what is to be done by the best knowers of the meaning of the Veda— / those men who perform that with effort are dear to me.

1.11.s:
varṇānāmanukampārthaṃ manniyogād virāṭ svayam /
svāyaṃbhuvo manurdhārmān munīnāṃ pūrvamuktavānā //
1.11.d:
वर्णानामनुकम्पार्थं मन्नियोगाद् विराट् स्वयम् ।
स्वायंभुवो मनुर्धार्मान् मुनीनां पूर्वमुक्तवाना ॥
1.11.m: Out of compassion for the classes, at my command, the cosmic ruler himself, / Manu Svāyambhuva, formerly declared the duties to the sages.

1.11.s:
śrutvā cānye 'pi munayastanmukhād dharmamuttamam /
cakrurdharmapratiṣṭhārthaṃ dharmaśāstrāṇi caiva hi //
1.11.d:
श्रुत्वा चान्ये ऽपि मुनयस्तन्मुखाद् धर्ममुत्तमम् ।
चक्रुर्धर्मप्रतिष्ठार्थं धर्मशास्त्राणि चैव हि ॥
1.11.m: And hearing that highest duty from his mouth, other sages too / composed treatises on duty for the establishment of duty.

1.11.s:
teṣu cāntarhiteṣvevaṃ yugānteṣu maharṣayaḥ /
brahmaṇo vacanāt tāni kariṣyanti yuge yuge //
1.11.d:
तेषु चान्तर्हितेष्वेवं युगान्तेषु महर्षयः ।
ब्रह्मणो वचनात् तानि करिष्यन्ति युगे युगे ॥
1.11.m: And when these have thus disappeared at the ends of cosmic ages, the great seers / will compose them age after age by the command of Brahmā.

1.11.s:
aṣṭādaśa purāṇāni vyāsena kathitāni tu /
niyogād brahmaṇo rājaṃsteṣu dharmaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ //
1.11.d:
अष्टादश पुराणानि व्यासेन कथितानि तु ।
नियोगाद् ब्रह्मणो राजंस्तेषु धर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
1.11.m: The eighteen Purāṇas were spoken by Vyāsa, / by the command of Brahmā, O king; in them duty is established.

1.11.s:
anyānyupapurāṇāni tacchiṣyaiḥ kathitāni tu /
yuge yuge 'tra sarveṣāṃ kartā vai dharmaśāstravit //
1.11.d:
अन्यान्युपपुराणानि तच्छिष्यैः कथितानि तु ।
युगे युगे ऽत्र सर्वेषां कर्ता वै धर्मशास्त्रवित् ॥
1.11.m: Other secondary Purāṇas were spoken by his disciples; / here, age after age, the author of them all is one who knows the treatises on duty.

1.11.s:
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chanda eva ca /
jyotiḥ śāstraṃ nyāyavidyā mīmāṃsā copabṛṃhaṇam //
1.11.d:
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्द एव च ।
ज्योतिः शास्त्रं न्यायविद्या मीमांसा चोपबृंहणम् ॥
1.11.m: Phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, and metrics, / astronomy, logic, and Mīmāṃsā as an elaboration—

1.11.s:
evaṃ caturdaśaitāni vidyāsthānāni sattama /
caturvedaiḥ sahoktāni dharmo nānyatra vidyate //
1.11.d:
एवं चतुर्दशैतानि विद्यास्थानानि सत्तम ।
चतुर्वेदैः सहोक्तानि धर्मो नान्यत्र विद्यते ॥
1.11.m: Thus these fourteen subjects of learning, O best of beings, / are declared along with the four Vedas; duty is not found elsewhere.

1.11.s:
evaṃ paitāmahaṃ dharmaṃ manuvyāsādayaḥ param /
sthāpayanti mamādeśād yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam //
1.11.d:
एवं पैतामहं धर्मं मनुव्यासादयः परम् ।
स्थापयन्ति ममादेशाद् यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ॥
1.11.m: Thus Manu, Vyāsa, and others establish the supreme duty / of the Grandfather by my command until the dissolution of all beings.

1.11.s:
brahmaṇā saha te sarve saṃprāpte pratisaṃcare /
parasyānte kṛtātmānaḥ praviśanti paraṃ padam //
1.11.d:
ब्रह्मणा सह ते सर्वे संप्राप्ते प्रतिसंचरे ।
परस्यान्ते कृतात्मानः प्रविशन्ति परं पदम् ॥
1.11.m: Together with Brahmā, when the universal dissolution arrives, / having perfected themselves, they all enter the supreme abode at the end of the Supreme [Brahman's life].

1.11.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena dharmārthaṃ vedamāśrayet /
dharmeṇa sahitaṃ jñānaṃ paraṃ brahma prakāśayet //
1.11.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन धर्मार्थं वेदमाश्रयेत् ।
धर्मेण सहितं ज्ञानं परं ब्रह्म प्रकाशयेत् ॥
1.11.m: Therefore, with every effort, one should resort to the Veda for the sake of dharma; / knowledge accompanied by dharma illuminates supreme Brahman.

1.11.s:
ye tu saṅgān parityajya māmeva śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ /
upāsate sadā bhaktyā yogamaiśvaramāsthitāḥ //
1.11.d:
ये तु सङ्गान् परित्यज्य मामेव शरणं गताः ।
उपासते सदा भक्त्या योगमैश्वरमास्थिताः ॥
1.11.m: Those, however, who abandon attachments, have taken refuge in me alone, / and constantly worship with devotion, established in the divine yoga—

1.11.s:
sarvabhūtadayāvantaḥ śāntā dāntā vimatsarāḥ /
amānino buddhimantastāpasāḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ //
1.11.d:
सर्वभूतदयावन्तः शान्ता दान्ता विमत्सराः ।
अमानिनो बुद्धिमन्तस्तापसाः शंसितव्रताः ॥
1.11.m: compassionate to all beings, peaceful, self-controlled, free from malice, / devoid of pride, wise, ascetic, observing strict vows,

1.11.s:
maccittā madgataprāṇā majjñānakathane ratāḥ /
saṃnyāsino gṛhasthāśca vanasthā brahmacāriṇaḥ //
1.11.d:
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा मज्ज्ञानकथने रताः ।
संन्यासिनो गृहस्थाश्च वनस्था ब्रह्मचारिणः ॥
1.11.m: their minds fixed on me, their life-breath offered to me, delighting in recounting knowledge of me, / whether renouncers, householders, forest-dwellers, or celibate students—

1.11.s:
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ māyātattvasamutthitam /
nāśayāmi tamaḥ kṛtsnaṃ jñānadīpane mā cirāt //
1.11.d:
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां मायातत्त्वसमुत्थितम् ।
नाशयामि तमः कृत्स्नं ज्ञानदीपने मा चिरात् ॥
1.11.m: for them, who are ever disciplined, I quickly destroy / with the lamp of knowledge all darkness arisen from the principle of illusory creative power.

1.11.s:
te sunirdhūtatamaso jñānenaikena manmayāḥ /
sadānandāstu saṃsāre na jāyante punaḥ punaḥ //
1.11.d:
ते सुनिर्धूततमसो ज्ञानेनैकेन मन्मयाः ।
सदानन्दास्तु संसारे न जायन्ते पुनः पुनः ॥
1.11.m: With darkness completely shaken off by unitary knowledge, imbued with me, / being ever blissful, they are not born again and again in saṃsāra.

1.11.s:
tasmāt sarvaprakāreṇa madbhakto matparāyaṇaḥ /
māmevārcaya sarvatra menayā saha saṃgataḥ //
1.11.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रकारेण मद्भक्तो मत्परायणः ।
मामेवार्चय सर्वत्र मेनया सह संगतः ॥
1.11.m: Therefore, by every means, devoted to me, making me your ultimate refuge, / worship me alone everywhere, together with Menā.

1.11.s:
aśakto yadi me dhyātumaiśvaraṃ rūpamavyayam /
tato me sakalaṃ rūpaṃ kālādyaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja //
1.11.d:
अशक्तो यदि मे ध्यातुमैश्वरं रूपमव्ययम् ।
ततो मे सकलं रूपं कालाद्यं शरणं व्रज ॥
1.11.m: If you are unable to meditate on my imperishable, sovereign form, / then take refuge in my manifested form with parts, beginning with Time.

1.11.s:
yad yat svarūpaṃ me tāta manaso gocaraṃ bhavet /
tanniṣṭhastatparo bhūtvā tadarcanaparo bhava //
1.11.d:
यद् यत् स्वरूपं मे तात मनसो गोचरं भवेत् ।
तन्निष्ठस्तत्परो भूत्वा तदर्चनपरो भव ॥
1.11.m: Whatever true form of mine, dear father, comes within the range of the mind, / intent on that, devoted to that, become dedicated to worshipping it.

1.11.s:
yattu me niṣkalaṃ rūpaṃ cinmātraṃ kevalaṃ śivam /
sarvopādhivinirmuktamanantamamṛtaṃ param //
1.11.d:
यत्तु मे निष्कलं रूपं चिन्मात्रं केवलं शिवम् ।
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तमनन्तममृतं परम् ॥
1.11.m: However, that form of mine which is partless, pure consciousness alone, Śiva, / completely freed from all limiting conditions, infinite, immortal, supreme—

1.11.s:
jñānenaikena tallabhyaṃ kleśena paramaṃ padam /
jñānameva prapaśyanto māmeva praviśanti te //
1.11.d:
ज्ञानेनैकेन तल्लभ्यं क्लेशेन परमं पदम् ।
ज्ञानमेव प्रपश्यन्तो मामेव प्रविशन्ति ते ॥
1.11.m: that supreme abode is to be attained by unitary knowledge with great difficulty; / perceiving knowledge alone, they enter me.

1.11.s:
tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ /
gacchantyapunarāvṛttiṃ jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ //
1.11.d:
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः ।
गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥
1.11.m: Their intellects fixed on That, their selves given to That, steadfast in That, holding That as their supreme goal, / with sins shaken off by knowledge, they go where there is no return.

1.11.s:
māmanāśritya paramaṃ nirvāṇamamalaṃ padam /
prāpyate na hi rājendra tato māṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja //
1.11.d:
मामनाश्रित्य परमं निर्वाणममलं पदम् ।
प्राप्यते न हि राजेन्द्र ततो मां शरणं व्रज ॥
1.11.m: Without resorting to me, the supreme, stainless state of nirvāṇa / cannot be attained, O king of kings; therefore, take refuge in me.

1.11.s:
ekatvena pṛthaktvena tathā cobhayato 'pi vā /
māmupāsya mahārāja tato yāsyāsi tatpadam //
1.11.d:
एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन तथा चोभयतो ऽपि वा ।
मामुपास्य महाराज ततो यास्यासि तत्पदम् ॥
1.11.m: Whether through unity, through diversity, or even through both, / having worshipped me, O great king, you will thereafter go to that realm.

1.11.s:
māmanāśritya tat tattvaṃ svabhāvavimalaṃ śivam /
jñāyate na hi rājendra tato māṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja //
1.11.d:
मामनाश्रित्य तत् तत्त्वं स्वभावविमलं शिवम् ।
ज्ञायते न हि राजेन्द्र ततो मां शरणं व्रज ॥
1.11.m: Without taking refuge in me, that reality, inherently pure, Śiva, / is not known, O king of kings; therefore, take refuge in me.

1.11.s:
tasmāt tvamakṣaraṃ rūpaṃ nityaṃ cārūpamaiśvaram /
ārādhaya prayatnena tato bandhaṃ prahāsyasi //
1.11.d:
तस्मात् त्वमक्षरं रूपं नित्यं चारूपमैश्वरम् ।
आराधय प्रयत्नेन ततो बन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥
1.11.m: Therefore, worship with effort the imperishable form, / the eternal, formless, and divine; then you will cast off bondage.

1.11.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā śivaṃ sarvatra sarvadā /
samārādhaya bhāvena tato yāsyasi tatpadam //
1.11.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा शिवं सर्वत्र सर्वदा ।
समाराधय भावेन ततो यास्यसि तत्पदम् ॥
1.11.m: Through action, mind, and speech, worship Śiva / everywhere, always, with devotional feeling; then you will go to that state.

1.11.s:
na vai paśyanti tat tattvaṃ mohitā mama māyayā /
anādyanantaṃ paramaṃ maheśvaramajaṃ śivam //
1.11.d:
न वै पश्यन्ति तत् तत्त्वं मोहिता मम मायया ।
अनाद्यनन्तं परमं महेश्वरमजं शिवम् ॥
1.11.m: Deluded by my illusory creative power, they do not see that reality: / the supreme Maheśvara, without beginning or end, unborn, Śiva,

1.11.s:
sarvabhūtātmabhūtasthaṃ sarvādhāraṃ nirañjanam /
nityānandaṃ nirābhāsaṃ nirguṇaṃ tamasaḥ param //
1.11.d:
सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थं सर्वाधारं निरञ्जनम् ।
नित्यानन्दं निराभासं निर्गुणं तमसः परम् ॥
1.11.m: dwelling in the inner self of all beings, the support of all, stainless, / eternally blissful, without illusory appearance, devoid of qualities, beyond darkness,

1.11.s:
advaitamacalaṃ brahma niṣkalaṃ niṣprapañcakam /
svasaṃvedyamavedyaṃ tat pare vyomni vyavasthitam //
1.11.d:
अद्वैतमचलं ब्रह्म निष्कलं निष्प्रपञ्चकम् ।
स्वसंवेद्यमवेद्यं तत् परे व्योम्नि व्यवस्थितम् ॥
1.11.m: non-dual, unmoving Brahman, partless, free from phenomenal expansion, / self-cognisable, unknowable [by others], situated in the supreme ether.

1.11.s:
sūkṣmeṇa tamasā nityaṃ veṣṭitā mama māyayā /
saṃsārasāgare ghore jāyante ca punaḥ punaḥ //
1.11.d:
सूक्ष्मेण तमसा नित्यं वेष्टिता मम मायया ।
संसारसागरे घोरे जायन्ते च पुनः पुनः ॥
1.11.m: Constantly enveloped by subtle darkness through my illusory creative power, / they are born again and again in the terrible ocean of saṃsāra.

1.11.s:
bhaktyā tvananyayā rājan samyag jñānena caiva hi /
anveṣṭavyaṃ hi tad brahma janmabandhanivṛttaye //
1.11.d:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया राजन् सम्यग् ज्ञानेन चैव हि ।
अन्वेष्टव्यं हि तद् ब्रह्म जन्मबन्धनिवृत्तये ॥
1.11.m: Indeed, through single-minded devotion, O king, and through correct knowledge alone / that Brahman is to be sought, for the cessation of the bondage of birth.

1.11.s:
ahaṅkāraṃ ca mātsaryaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham /
adharmābhiniveśaṃ ca tyaktvā vairāgyamāsthitaḥ //
1.11.d:
अहङ्कारं च मात्सर्यं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
अधर्माभिनिवेशं च त्यक्त्वा वैराग्यमास्थितः ॥
1.11.m: Having abandoned egoism, envy, desire, anger, possessiveness, / and inclination toward unrighteousness, having taken recourse to dispassion,

1.11.s:
sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani /
anvīkṣya cātmanātmānaṃ brahmabhūyāya kalpate //
1.11.d:
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
अन्वीक्ष्य चात्मनात्मानं ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
1.11.m: and perceiving the self in all beings and all beings in the self, / observing the Self by means of the self, one becomes fit for becoming Brahman.

1.11.s:
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā sarvabhūtābhayapradaḥ /
aiśvarīṃ paramāṃ bhaktiṃ vindetānanyagāminīm //
1.11.d:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा सर्वभूताभयप्रदः ।
ऐश्वरीं परमां भक्तिं विन्देतानन्यगामिनीम् ॥
1.11.m: Having become Brahman, of tranquil mind, granting fearlessness to all beings, / one obtains supreme, sovereign devotion that is directed to none other.

1.11.s:
vīkṣate tat paraṃ tattvamaiśvaraṃ brahmaniṣkalam /
sarvasaṃsāranirmukto brahmaṇeyavāvatiṣṭhate //
1.11.d:
वीक्षते तत् परं तत्त्वमैश्वरं ब्रह्मनिष्कलम् ।
सर्वसंसारनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मणेयवावतिष्ठते ॥
1.11.m: He beholds that supreme reality, sovereign, partless Brahman; / completely liberated from all saṃsāra, he abides in Brahman alone.

1.11.s:
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāyaṃ parasya paramaḥ śivaḥ /
anantasyāvyayasyaikaḥ svātmādhāro maheśvaraḥ //
1.11.d:
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठायं परस्य परमः शिवः ।
अनन्तस्याव्ययस्यैकः स्वात्माधारो महेश्वरः ॥
1.11.m: For supreme Śiva is the foundation of supreme Brahman; / the infinite, imperishable, sole Maheśvara is supported by his own Self.

1.11.s:
jñānena karmayogena bhaktiyogena vā nṛpa /
sarvasaṃsāramuktyarthamīśvaraṃ satataṃ śraya //
1.11.d:
ज्ञानेन कर्मयोगेन भक्तियोगेन वा नृप ।
सर्वसंसारमुक्त्यर्थमीश्वरं सततं श्रय ॥
1.11.m: Through knowledge, through the yoga of action, or through the yoga of devotion, O king, / constantly take refuge in the Lord for the sake of release from all saṃsāra.

1.11.s:
eṣa guhyopadeśaste mayā datto girīśvara /
anvīkṣya caitadakhilaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ kartumarhasi //
1.11.d:
एष गुह्योपदेशस्ते मया दत्तो गिरीश्वर ।
अन्वीक्ष्य चैतदखिलं यथेष्टं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.11.m: This secret teaching has been given to you by me, O lord of mountains; / having examined all of this, you may act as you wish.

1.11.s:
ahaṃ vai yācitā devaiḥ saṃjātā parameśvarāt /
vinindya dakṣaṃ pitaraṃ maheśvaravinindakam //
1.11.d:
अहं वै याचिता देवैः संजाता परमेश्वरात् ।
विनिन्द्य दक्षं पितरं महेश्वरविनिन्दकम् ॥
1.11.m: Implored by the gods, I arose from the Supreme Lord / after reproaching Dakṣa, my father, who had reviled Maheśvara.

1.11.s:
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya tavārādhanakāraṇāt /
menādehasamutpannā tvāmeva pitaraṃ śritā //
1.11.d:
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय तवाराधनकारणात् ।
मेनादेहसमुत्पन्ना त्वामेव पितरं श्रिता ॥
1.11.m: For the purpose of establishing dharma, and on account of your worship, / born from the body of Menā, I have taken you alone as my father.

1.11.s:
sa tvaṃ niyogād devasya brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
pridāsyase māṃ rudrāya svayaṃvarasamāgame //
1.11.d:
स त्वं नियोगाद् देवस्य ब्रह्मणः परमात्मनः ।
प्रिदास्यसे मां रुद्राय स्वयंवरसमागमे ॥
1.11.m: You yourself, by the command of God Brahmā, the Supreme Self, / shall give me to Rudra at the gathering of the svayaṃvara.

1.11.s:
tatsaṃbandhācca te rājan sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ /
tvāṃ namasyanti vai tāta prasīdati ca śaṅkaraḥ //
1.11.d:
तत्संबन्धाच्च ते राजन् सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ।
त्वां नमस्यन्ति वै तात प्रसीदति च शङ्करः ॥
1.11.m: And on account of that alliance, O king, all the gods along with Indra / will surely bow down to you, dear father, and Śaṅkara will be pleased.

1.11.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena māṃ viddhīśvaragocarām /
saṃpūjya devamīśānaṃ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja //
1.11.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन मां विद्धीश्वरगोचराम् ।
संपूज्य देवमीशानं शरण्यं शरणं व्रज ॥
1.11.m: Therefore, by every effort know me as accessible through the Lord; / having worshipped God Īśāna, take refuge in the one worthy of refuge."

1.11.s:
sa evamukto bhagavān devadevyā girīśvaraḥ /
praṇamya śirasā devīṃ prāñjaliḥ punarabravīt //
1.11.d:
स एवमुक्तो भगवान् देवदेव्या गिरीश्वरः ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवीं प्राञ्जलिः पुनरब्रवीत् ॥
1.11.m: Thus addressed by the Goddess of gods, the lord of mountains, / having bowed his head to the Goddess, with folded hands spoke again:

1.11.s:
vistareṇa maheśāni yogaṃ māheśvaraṃ param /
jñānaṃ caivātmano yogaṃ sādhanāni pracakṣva me //
1.11.d:
विस्तरेण महेशानि योगं माहेश्वरं परम् ।
ज्ञानं चैवात्मनो योगं साधनानि प्रचक्ष्व मे ॥
1.11.m: "In detail, O supreme ruler, explain to me the supreme yoga of Maheśvara, / knowledge, the yoga of the Self, and the spiritual means."

1.11.s:
tasyaitat paramaṃ jñānamātmayogamanuttamam /
yathāvad vyājahāreśāsādhanānica vistarāt //
1.11.d:
तस्यैतत् परमं ज्ञानमात्मयोगमनुत्तमम् ।
यथावद् व्याजहारेशासाधनानिच विस्तरात् ॥
1.11.m: To him the Ruler faithfully proclaimed this supreme knowledge, / the unexcelled yoga of the Self, and the spiritual means in full detail.

1.11.s:
niśamya vadanāmbhojād girīndro lokapūjitaḥ /
lokamātuḥ paraṃ jñānaṃ yogāsakto 'bhavatpunaḥ //
1.11.d:
निशम्य वदनाम्भोजाद् गिरीन्द्रो लोकपूजितः ।
लोकमातुः परं ज्ञानं योगासक्तो ऽभवत्पुनः ॥
1.11.m: Having heard from the lotus mouth of the Mother of the Worlds the supreme knowledge, / the lord of mountains, revered by the world, became devoted to yoga once again.

1.11.s:
pradadau ca maheśāya pārvatīṃ bhāgyagauravāt /
niyogād brahmaṇaḥ sādhvīṃ devānāṃ caiva saṃnidhau //
1.11.d:
प्रददौ च महेशाय पार्वतीं भाग्यगौरवात् ।
नियोगाद् ब्रह्मणः साध्वीं देवानां चैव संनिधौ ॥
1.11.m: And on account of the greatness of his good fortune, by the command of Brahmā, / he gave the virtuous Pārvatī to Maheśa in the presence of the gods.

1.11.s:
ya imaṃ paṭhate 'dhyāyaṃ devyā māhātmyakīrtanam /
śivasya saṃnidhau bhaktyā sucistadbhāvabhāvitaḥ //
1.11.d:
य इमं पठते ऽध्यायं देव्या माहात्म्यकीर्तनम् ।
शिवस्य संनिधौ भक्त्या सुचिस्तद्भावभावितः ॥
1.11.m: Whoever recites this chapter celebrating the majesty of the Goddess, / pure, in the presence of Śiva, with devotion, absorbed in contemplation of Her,

1.11.s:
sarvapāpavinirmukto divyayogasamanvitaḥ /
ullaṅghya brahmaṇo lokandevyāḥ sthānamavāpnuyāt //
1.11.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो दिव्ययोगसमन्वितः ।
उल्लङ्घ्य ब्रह्मणो लोकन्देव्याः स्थानमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.11.m: completely freed from all sins, endowed with divine yoga, / having transcended the worlds of Brahmā, attains the abode of the Goddess.

1.11.s:
yaścaitat paṭhate stotraṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ samīpataḥ /
devyāḥ samāhitamanāḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
1.11.d:
यश्चैतत् पठते स्तोत्रं ब्राह्मणानां समीपतः ।
देव्याः समाहितमनाः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.11.m: And whoever recites this hymn of praise in the presence of brāhmaṇas, / with a concentrated mind fixed on the Goddess, is delivered from all sins.

1.11.s:
nāmnāmaṣṭasahastraṃ tu devyā yat samudīritam /
jñātvār'kamaṇḍalagatāṃ saṃbhāvya parameśvarīm //
1.11.d:
नाम्नामष्टसहस्त्रं तु देव्या यत् समुदीरितम् ।
ज्ञात्वार्ऽकमण्डलगतां संभाव्य परमेश्वरीम् ॥
1.11.m: The eight thousand names of the Goddess that have been proclaimed— / having known and contemplated the Supreme Goddess residing in the solar orb,

1.11.s:
abhyarcya gandhapuṣpādyairbhaktiyogasamanvitaḥ /
saṃsmaran paramaṃ bhāvaṃ devyā māheśvaraṃ param //
1.11.d:
अभ्यर्च्य गन्धपुष्पाद्यैर्भक्तियोगसमन्वितः ।
संस्मरन् परमं भावं देव्या माहेश्वरं परम् ॥
1.11.m: having worshipped her with perfumes, flowers, and the like, endowed with the yoga of devotion, / recollecting the supreme sovereign state of the Goddess,

1.11.s:
ananyamānaso nityaṃ japedāmaraṇād dvijaḥ /
so 'ntakāle smṛtiṃ labdhvāparaṃ brahmādhigacchati //
1.11.d:
अनन्यमानसो नित्यं जपेदामरणाद् द्विजः ।
सो ऽन्तकाले स्मृतिं लब्ध्वापरं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥
1.11.m: if a twice-born person constantly recites it until death with undivided mind, / he, having attained remembrance at the time of death, reaches supreme Brahman.

1.11.s:
athavā jāyate vipro brāhmaṇānāṃ kule śucau /
pūrvasaṃskāramāhātmyād brahmavidyāmavāpya saḥ //
1.11.d:
अथवा जायते विप्रो ब्राह्मणानां कुले शुचौ ।
पूर्वसंस्कारमाहात्म्याद् ब्रह्मविद्यामवाप्य सः ॥
1.11.m: Or else, the brāhmaṇa is born in a pure family of brāhmaṇas, / and, having obtained the knowledge of Brahman through the power of previous impressions,

1.11.s:
saṃprāpya yogaṃ paramaṃ divyaṃ tat pārameśvaram /
śāntaḥ sarvagāto bhūtvā śivasāyujyamānapnuyāt //
1.11.d:
संप्राप्य योगं परमं दिव्यं तत् पारमेश्वरम् ।
शान्तः सर्वगातो भूत्वा शिवसायुज्यमानप्नुयात् ॥
1.11.m: having attained that highest, divine yoga belonging to the Supreme Lord, / tranquil and omnipresent, he would attain complete union with Śiva.

1.11.s:
pratyekaṃ cātha nāmāni juhuyāt savanatrayam /
pūtanādikṛtairdeṣairgrahadoṣaiśca mucyate //
1.11.d:
प्रत्येकं चाथ नामानि जुहुयात् सवनत्रयम् ।
पूतनादिकृतैर्देषैर्ग्रहदोषैश्च मुच्यते ॥
1.11.m: And if one should make offerings with each of the names at the three daily oblations, / he is freed from the afflictions caused by Pūtanā and the like, and from planetary afflictions.

1.11.s:
japed vāharaharnityaṃ saṃvatsaramatandritaḥ /
śrīkāmaḥ pārvatīṃ devīṃ pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ //
1.11.d:
जपेद् वाहरहर्नित्यं संवत्सरमतन्द्रितः ।
श्रीकामः पार्वतीं देवीं पूजयित्वा विधानतः ॥
1.11.m: Or, desiring prosperity, he should recite it every day unwearied for a year, / having worshipped the goddess Pārvatī according to the ritual rules,

1.11.s:
saṃpūjya pārśvataḥ śaṃbhuṃ trinetraṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ /
labhate mahatīṃ lakṣmīṃ mahādevaprasādataḥ //
1.11.d:
संपूज्य पार्श्वतः शंभुं त्रिनेत्रं भक्तिसंयुतः ।
लभते महतीं लक्ष्मीं महादेवप्रसादतः ॥
1.11.m: and having worshipped the three-eyed Śambhu at her side with devotion; / he obtains great prosperity through the grace of Mahādeva.

1.11.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena japtavyaṃ hi dvijātibhiḥ /
sarvapāpānodārthaṃ devyā nāma sahastrakam //
1.11.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन जप्तव्यं हि द्विजातिभिः ।
सर्वपापानोदार्थं देव्या नाम सहस्त्रकम् ॥
1.11.m: Therefore, the thousand names of the goddess / must be recited with every effort by the twice-born for the removal of all sins.

1.11.s:
prasaṅgāt kathitaṃ viprā devyā māhātmyamuttamam /
ataḥ paraṃ prajāsargaṃ bhṛgvādīnāṃ nibodhata //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge ekādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.11.d:
प्रसङ्गात् कथितं विप्रा देव्या माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ।
अतः परं प्रजासर्गं भृग्वादीनां निबोधत ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे एकादशो ऽध्यायः
1.11.m:
This excellent majesty of the goddess has been recounted incidentally, O brāhmaṇas. / Henceforth, understand the generation of offspring of Bhṛgu and the others.

Thus ends the eleventh chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.12.s:
sūta uvāca
bhṛgoḥ khyātyāṃ samutpannā lakṣmīrnārāyaṇapriyā /
devau dhātāvidhātārau merorjāmātarau tathā //
1.12.d:
सूत उवाच
भृगोः ख्यात्यां समुत्पन्ना लक्ष्मीर्नारायणप्रिया ।
देवौ धाताविधातारौ मेरोर्जामातरौ तथा ॥
1.12.m: Sūta said: / From Khyāti by Bhṛgu was born Lakṣmī, beloved of Nārāyaṇa, / and the two gods Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, as well as the two sons-in-law of Meru.

1.12.s:
āyatirniyatirmeroḥ kanye caiva mahātmanaḥ /
dhātāvidhātroste bhārye tayorjātau sutāvubhau //
1.12.d:
आयतिर्नियतिर्मेरोः कन्ये चैव महात्मनः ।
धाताविधात्रोस्ते भार्ये तयोर्जातौ सुतावुभौ ॥
1.12.m: Āyati and Niyati were the two daughters of the great-souled Meru; / they were the wives of Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ. To the two of them were born two sons:

1.12.s:
prāṇaścaiva mṛkaṇḍuśca mārkaṇḍeyo mṛkaṇḍutaḥ /
tathā vedaśirā nāma prāṇasya dyutimān sutaḥ //
1.12.d:
प्राणश्चैव मृकण्डुश्च मार्कण्डेयो मृकण्डुतः ।
तथा वेदशिरा नाम प्राणस्य द्युतिमान् सुतः ॥
1.12.m: Prāṇa and Mṛkaṇḍu; and Mārkaṇḍeya was from Mṛkaṇḍu. / Likewise, the radiant son named Vedaśiras was of Prāṇa.

1.12.s:
marīcerapi saṃbhūtiḥ paurṇamāsamasūyata /
kanyācatuṣṭayaṃ caiva sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam //
1.12.d:
मरीचेरपि संभूतिः पौर्णमासमसूयत ।
कन्याचतुष्टयं चैव सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् ॥
1.12.m: To Marīci also, Saṃbhūti gave birth to Paurṇamāsa, / and to four daughters endowed with all auspicious marks:

1.12.s:
tuṣṭirjyeṣṭhā tathā vṛṣṭiḥ kṛṣṭiścāpacitistathā /
virajāḥ parvaścaiva paurṇamāsasya tau sutau //
1.12.d:
तुष्टिर्ज्येष्ठा तथा वृष्टिः कृष्टिश्चापचितिस्तथा ।
विरजाः पर्वश्चैव पौर्णमासस्य तौ सुतौ ॥
1.12.m: Tuṣṭi, Jyeṣṭhā, Vṛṣṭi, and Kṛṣṭi, as well as Apaciti. / Virajas and Parvan were the two sons of Paurṇamāsa.

1.12.s:
kṣamā tu suṣuve putrān pulahasya prajāpateḥ /
kardamaṃ ca varīyāṃsaṃ sahiṣṇuṃ munisattamam //
1.12.d:
क्षमा तु सुषुवे पुत्रान् पुलहस्य प्रजापतेः ।
कर्दमं च वरीयांसं सहिष्णुं मुनिसत्तमम् ॥
1.12.m: And Kṣamā gave birth to the sons of the lord of creatures Pulaha: / Kardama the elder, Sahiṣṇu the best of sages,

1.12.s:
tathaiva ca kanīyāsaṃ taponirdhūtakalpaṣam /
anasūyā tathaivātrerjajñe putrānakalpaṣān //
1.12.d:
तथैव च कनीयासं तपोनिर्धूतकल्पषम् ।
अनसूया तथैवात्रेर्जज्ञे पुत्रानकल्पषान् ॥
1.12.m: and likewise a younger brother whose sins were shaken off by austerity. / Similarly, Anasūyā bore sinless sons to Atri:

1.12.s:
somaṃ durvāsasaṃ caiva dattātreyaṃ ca yoginam /
smṛtiścāṅgirasaḥ putrīrjajñe lakṣaṇasaṃyutāḥ //
1.12.d:
सोमं दुर्वाससं चैव दत्तात्रेयं च योगिनम् ।
स्मृतिश्चाङ्गिरसः पुत्रीर्जज्ञे लक्षणसंयुताः ॥
1.12.m: Soma, Durvāsas, and the yogin Dattātreya. / And Smṛti bore to Aṅgiras daughters endowed with auspicious marks:

1.12.s:
sinīvālīṃ kuhūṃ caiva rākāmanumatiṃ tathā /
prītyāṃ pulastyo bhagavān dattātrimasṛjat prabhuḥ //
1.12.d:
सिनीवालीं कुहूं चैव राकामनुमतिं तथा ।
प्रीत्यां पुलस्त्यो भगवान् दत्तात्रिमसृजत् प्रभुः ॥
1.12.m: Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, and Anumati. / In Prīti the lord, venerable Pulastya, begot Dattātri—

1.12.s:
pūrvajanmani so 'gastyaḥ smṛtaḥ svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare /
vedabāhuṃ tathā kanyāṃ sannatiṃ nāma nāmataḥ //
1.12.d:
पूर्वजन्मनि सो ऽगस्त्यः स्मृतः स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे ।
वेदबाहुं तथा कन्यां सन्नतिं नाम नामतः ॥
1.12.m: he is remembered as Agastya in a previous birth in the Svāyambhuva cosmic era— / and likewise Vedabāhu, and a daughter named Sannati.

1.12.s:
putrāṇāṃ ṣaṣṭisāhastraṃ saṃtatiḥ suṣuve kratoḥ /
te cordhvaretasaḥ sarve bālakhilyā iti smṛtāḥ //
1.12.d:
पुत्राणां षष्टिसाहस्त्रं संततिः सुषुवे क्रतोः ।
ते चोर्ध्वरेतसः सर्वे बालखिल्या इति स्मृताः ॥
1.12.m: Saṃtati bore sixty thousand sons to Kratu; / they were all celibate, remembered as the Bālakhilyas.

1.12.s:
vasiṣṭhaśca tathorjāyāṃ saptaputrānajījanat /
kanyāṃ ca puṇḍarīkākṣāṃ sarveśobhāsamanvitām //
1.12.d:
वसिष्ठश्च तथोर्जायां सप्तपुत्रानजीजनत् ।
कन्यां च पुण्डरीकाक्षां सर्वेशोभासमन्विताम् ॥
1.12.m: And Vasiṣṭha begot seven sons in Ūrjā, / and a lotus-eyed daughter endowed with all beauty:

1.12.s:
rajohaścordhvabāhuśca savanaścānaghastathā /
sutapāḥ śukra ityete sapta putrā mahaujasaḥ //
1.12.d:
रजोहश्चोर्ध्वबाहुश्च सवनश्चानघस्तथा ।
सुतपाः शुक्र इत्येते सप्त पुत्रा महौजसः ॥
1.12.m: Rajas, Ūrdhvabāhu, Savana, Anagha, / Sutapas, and Śukra—these were the seven sons of great splendour.

1.12.s:
yo 'sau rudrātmako vahnirbrahmaṇastanayo dvijāḥ /
svāhā tasmāt sutān lebhe trīnudārān mahaujasaḥ //
1.12.d:
यो ऽसौ रुद्रात्मको वह्निर्ब्रह्मणस्तनयो द्विजाः ।
स्वाहा तस्मात् सुतान् लेभे त्रीनुदारान् महौजसः ॥
1.12.m: That fire whose nature is Rudra, who is the son of Brahmā, O twice-born ones— / Svāhā obtained from him three noble sons of great splendour:

1.12.s:
pāvakaḥ pavamānaśca śuciragniśca te trayaḥ /
nirmathyaḥ pavamānaḥ syād vaidyutaḥ pāvakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.12.d:
पावकः पवमानश्च शुचिरग्निश्च ते त्रयः ।
निर्मथ्यः पवमानः स्याद् वैद्युतः पावकः स्मृतः ॥
1.12.m: Pāvaka, Pavamāna, and Śuci—these are the three fires. / Pavamāna is [the fire] produced by friction; Pāvaka is remembered as lightning fire;

1.12.s:
yaścāsau tapate sūryaḥ śuciragnistvasau smṛtaḥ /
teṣāṃ tu saṃtatāvanye catvāriṃśca pañca ca //
1.12.d:
यश्चासौ तपते सूर्यः शुचिरग्निस्त्वसौ स्मृतः ।
तेषां तु संततावन्ये चत्वारिंश्च पञ्च च ॥
1.12.m: and the sun that blazes is remembered as the fire Śuci. / In their lineage were forty-five others.

1.12.s:
pāvakaḥ pavamānaśca śucisteṣāṃ pitā ca yaḥ /
ete caikonapañcāśad vahnayaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
1.12.d:
पावकः पवमानश्च शुचिस्तेषां पिता च यः ।
एते चैकोनपञ्चाशद् वह्नयः परिकीर्तितः ॥
1.12.m: Pāvaka, Pavamāna, and Śuci, and he who is their father— / these are proclaimed as the forty-nine fires.

1.12.s:
sarve tapasvinaḥ proktāḥ sarve yajñeṣu bhāginaḥ /
rudrātmakāḥ smṛtāḥ sarve tripuṇḍrāṅkitamastakāḥ //
1.12.d:
सर्वे तपस्विनः प्रोक्ताः सर्वे यज्ञेषु भागिनः ।
रुद्रात्मकाः स्मृताः सर्वे त्रिपुण्ड्राङ्कितमस्तकाः ॥
1.12.m: All are declared to be ascetic; all have shares in sacrifices; / all are remembered as having the nature of Rudra, their foreheads marked with the three ash-stripes.

1.12.s:
ayajvānaśca yajvānaḥ pitaro brahmaṇaḥ smṛtāḥ /
agniṣvāttā barhiṣado dvidhā teṣāṃ vyavasthitiḥ //
1.12.d:
अयज्वानश्च यज्वानः पितरो ब्रह्मणः स्मृताः ।
अग्निष्वात्ता बर्हिषदो द्विधा तेषां व्यवस्थितिः ॥
1.12.m: Non-sacrificers and sacrificers are remembered as the ancestors of Brahmā; / their division is twofold: the Agniṣvāttas and the Barhiṣads.

1.12.s:
tebhyaḥ svadhā sutāṃ jajñe menāṃ vaitaraṇīṃ tathā /
te ubhe brahmavādinyau yoginyau munisattamāḥ //
1.12.d:
तेभ्यः स्वधा सुतां जज्ञे मेनां वैतरणीं तथा ।
ते उभे ब्रह्मवादिन्यौ योगिन्यौ मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
1.12.m: From them Svadhā bore two daughters, Menā and Vaitaraṇī; / both were teachers of Brahman and yoginīs, O best of sages.

1.12.s:
asūta menā mainākaṃ krauñcaṃ tasyānujaṃ tathā /
gaṅgā himavato jajñe sarvalokaikapāvanī //
1.12.d:
असूत मेना मैनाकं क्रौञ्चं तस्यानुजं तथा ।
गङ्गा हिमवतो जज्ञे सर्वलोकैकपावनी ॥
1.12.m: Menā gave birth to Maināka, and Krauñca his younger brother. / Gaṅgā, the sole purifier of all the worlds, was born from Himavat.

1.12.s:
svayogāgnibalād devīṃ lebhe putrīṃ maheśvarīṃ /
yathāvat kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ devyā māhātmyamuttamam //
1.12.d:
स्वयोगाग्निबलाद् देवीं लेभे पुत्रीं महेश्वरीं ।
यथावत् कथितं पूर्वं देव्या माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥
1.12.m: By the power of the fire of her own yoga she obtained the goddess, the Great Sovereign, as her daughter; / the excellent majesty of the goddess has been recounted before as it truly was.

1.12.s:
eṣā dakṣasya kanyānāṃ mayāpatyānusaṃtatiḥ /
vyākhyātā bhavatāmadya manoḥ sṛṣṭiṃ nibodhata //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.12.d:
एषा दक्षस्य कन्यानां मयापत्यानुसंततिः ।
व्याख्याता भवतामद्य मनोः सृष्टिं निबोधत ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे द्वादशो ऽध्यायः
1.12.m:
This lineage of descendants of the daughters of Dakṣa / has now been explained by me to you. Understand the creation of Manu.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.13.s:
sūta uvāca
priyavratottānapādau manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasya tu /
dharmajñau sumahāvīryau śatarūpā vyajījanat //
1.13.d:
सूत उवाच
प्रियव्रतोत्तानपादौ मनोः स्वायंभुवस्य तु ।
धर्मज्ञौ सुमहावीर्यौ शतरूपा व्यजीजनत् ॥
1.13.m: Sūta said: / Śatarūpā gave birth to Priyavrata and Uttānapāda, / sons of Manu Svāyambhuva, knowers of duty, possessed of very great valour.

1.13.s:
tatastūttānapādasya dhruvo nāma suto 'bhavat /
bhakto nārāyaṇe deve prāptavān sthānamuttamam //
1.13.d:
ततस्तूत्तानपादस्य ध्रुवो नाम सुतो ऽभवत् ।
भक्तो नारायणे देवे प्राप्तवान् स्थानमुत्तमम् ॥
1.13.m: Then to Uttānapāda was born a son named Dhruva, / devoted to the god Nārāyaṇa, who attained the supreme abode.

1.13.s:
dhruvāt śliṣṭiñca bhavyaṃ ca bhāryā śambhurvyajāyata /
śliṣṭerādhatta succhāyā pañca putrānakalpaṣān //
1.13.d:
ध्रुवात् श्लिष्टिञ्च भव्यं च भार्या शम्भुर्व्यजायत ।
श्लिष्टेराधत्त सुच्छाया पञ्च पुत्रानकल्पषान् ॥
1.13.m: From Dhruva his wife Śambhu gave birth to Śliṣṭi and Bhavya; / and Succhāyā bore five sinless sons to Śliṣṭi.

1.13.s:
vasiṣṭhavacanād devī tapastaptvā suduścaram /
ārādhya puruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ śālagrāme janārdanam //
1.13.d:
वसिष्ठवचनाद् देवी तपस्तप्त्वा सुदुश्चरम् ।
आराध्य पुरुषं विष्णुं शालग्रामे जनार्दनम् ॥
1.13.m: At the instruction of Vasiṣṭha, having performed severe austerity, / that lady worshipped Viṣṇu, the Spirit, Janārdana, at Śālagrāma,

1.13.s:
ripuṃ ripuñjayaṃ vipraṃ vṛkalaṃ vṛṣatejasam /
nārāyaṇaparān śuddhān svadharmaparipālakān //
1.13.d:
रिपुं रिपुञ्जयं विप्रं वृकलं वृषतेजसम् ।
नारायणपरान् शुद्धान् स्वधर्मपरिपालकान् ॥
1.13.m: [and bore] Ripu, Ripuñjaya, Vipra, Vṛkala, and Vṛṣatejas, / devoted to Nārāyaṇa, pure, protectors of their own duty.

1.13.s:
riporādhatta bṛhatī cakṣuṣaṃ sarvatejasam /
so 'jījanat puṣkariṇyāṃ vairaṇyāṃ cākṣuṣaṃ manum /
prajāpaterātmajāyāṃ vīraṇasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.13.d:
रिपोराधत्त बृहती चक्षुषं सर्वतेजसम् ।
सो ऽजीजनत् पुष्करिण्यां वैरण्यां चाक्षुषं मनुम् ।
प्रजापतेरात्मजायां वीरणस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.13.m: Bṛhatī bore to Ripu the all-radiant Cakṣus; / he begot Cakṣuṣa Manu in Puṣkariṇī Vairaṇī, / the daughter of the great-souled lord of creatures Vīraṇa.

1.13.s:
manorajāyanta daśa naḍvalāyāṃ mahaujasaḥ /
kanyāyāṃ sumahāvīryā vairājasya prajāpateḥ //
1.13.d:
मनोरजायन्त दश नड्वलायां महौजसः ।
कन्यायां सुमहावीर्या वैराजस्य प्रजापतेः ॥
1.13.m: Ten sons of great splendour and very great valour were born to Manu / in Naḍvalā, the daughter of the lord of creatures Vairāja:

1.13.s:
ūruḥ pūruḥ śatadyumnastapasvī satyavāk śuciḥ /
agniṣṭudatirātraśca sudyumnaścābhimanyukaḥ //
1.13.d:
ऊरुः पूरुः शतद्युम्नस्तपस्वी सत्यवाक् शुचिः ।
अग्निष्टुदतिरात्रश्च सुद्युम्नश्चाभिमन्युकः ॥
1.13.m: Ūru, Pūru, Śatadyumna, the ascetic Satyavāc, Śuci, / Agniṣṭut, Atirātra, Sudyumna, and Abhimanyuka.

1.13.s:
ūrorajanayat putrān ṣaḍāgneyī mahābalān /
aṅgaṃ sumanasaṃ svātiṃ kratumaṅgirasaṃ śivam //
1.13.d:
ऊरोरजनयत् पुत्रान् षडाग्नेयी महाबलान् ।
अङ्गं सुमनसं स्वातिं क्रतुमङ्गिरसं शिवम् ॥
1.13.m: Āgneyī bore to Ūru six sons of great strength: / Aṅga, Sumanas, Svāti, Kratu, Aṅgiras, and Śiva.

1.13.s:
aṅgād veno 'bhavat paścād bainyo venādajāyata /
yo 'sau pṛthuriti khyātaḥ prajāpālo mahābalaḥ //
1.13.d:
अङ्गाद् वेनो ऽभवत् पश्चाद् बैन्यो वेनादजायत ।
यो ऽसौ पृथुरिति ख्यातः प्रजापालो महाबलः ॥
1.13.m: From Aṅga, Vena was born afterwards; from Vena, Pṛthu son of Vena was born, / he who is renowned as Pṛthu, the protector of subjects, of great strength,

1.13.s:
yena dugdhā mahī pūrvaṃ prājānāṃ hitakāraṇāt /
niyogād brahmaṇaḥ sārdhaṃ devendreṇa mahaujasā //
1.13.d:
येन दुग्धा मही पूर्वं प्राजानां हितकारणात् ।
नियोगाद् ब्रह्मणः सार्धं देवेन्द्रेण महौजसा ॥
1.13.m: by whom the earth was milked formerly for the benefit of creatures, / by the appointment of Brahmā, together with the mighty lord of gods.

1.13.s:
venaputrasya vitate purā paitāmahe makhe /
sūtaḥ paurāṇiko jajñe māyārūpaḥ svayaṃ hariḥ //
1.13.d:
वेनपुत्रस्य वितते पुरा पैतामहे मखे ।
सूतः पौराणिको जज्ञे मायारूपः स्वयं हरिः ॥
1.13.m: Anciently, when the sacrificial session of Brahmā held by the son of Vena was spread out, / the Sūta who relates the Purāṇas was born, who was Hari himself in illusory form.

1.13.s:
pravaktā sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ dharmajño guṇavatsalaḥ /
taṃ māṃ nitta muniśreṣṭhāḥ pūrvodbhūtaṃ sanātanam //
1.13.d:
प्रवक्ता सर्वशास्त्राणां धर्मज्ञो गुणवत्सलः ।
तं मां नित्त मुनिश्रेष्ठाः पूर्वोद्भूतं सनातनम् ॥
1.13.m: He is the proclaimer of all scriptures, knower of duty, lover of virtues; / know me, O best of sages, to be that ancient, eternal one.

1.13.s:
asmin manvantare vyāsaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ svayam /
śrāvayāmāsa māṃ prītyā purāṇaṃ puruṣo hariḥ //
1.13.d:
अस्मिन् मन्वन्तरे व्यासः कृष्णद्वैपायनः स्वयम् ।
श्रावयामास मां प्रीत्या पुराणं पुरुषो हरिः ॥
1.13.m: In this cosmic era of a Manu, Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana himself, / the Spirit, Hari, lovingly caused me to hear the Purāṇa.

1.13.s:
madanvaye tu ye sūtāḥ saṃbhūtā vedavarjitāḥ /
teṣāṃ purāṇavaktṛtvaṃ vṛttirāsīdajājñayā //
1.13.d:
मदन्वये तु ये सूताः संभूता वेदवर्जिताः ।
तेषां पुराणवक्तृत्वं वृत्तिरासीदजाज्ञया ॥
1.13.m: Those sūtas who were born in my lineage, destitute of the Vedas— / reciting the Purāṇas became their livelihood by the command of the Unborn.

1.13.s:
sa tu vainyaḥ pṛthurdhomān satyasaṃdho jitendriyaḥ /
sārvabhaumo mahātejāḥ svadharmaparipālakaḥ //
1.13.d:
स तु वैन्यः पृथुर्धोमान् सत्यसंधो जितेन्द्रियः ।
सार्वभौमो महातेजाः स्वधर्मपरिपालकः ॥
1.13.m: That Pṛthu, son of Vena, was wise, true to his promise, of conquered senses, / a universal emperor of great splendour, a protector of his own duty.

1.13.s:
tasya bālyāt prabhṛtyeva bhaktirnārāyaṇe 'bhavat /
govardhanagiriṃ prāpya tapastepe jitendriyaḥ //
1.13.d:
तस्य बाल्यात् प्रभृत्येव भक्तिर्नारायणे ऽभवत् ।
गोवर्धनगिरिं प्राप्य तपस्तेपे जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.13.m: From his very childhood, he had devotion to Nārāyaṇa. / Having reached Mount Govardhana, he performed austerities with conquered senses.

1.13.s:
tapasā bhagavān prītaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
āgatya devo rājānaṃ prāha dāmodaraḥ svayam //
1.13.d:
तपसा भगवान् प्रीतः शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ।
आगत्य देवो राजानं प्राह दामोदरः स्वयम् ॥
1.13.m: Pleased by his austerity, the Blessed One who bears the conch, discus, and mace, / the god Dāmodara himself arrived and addressed the king:

1.13.s:
dhramikau rūpasaṃpannau sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varau /
matprasādādasaṃdigdhaṃ putrau tava bhaviṣyataḥ /
ekamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ svakīyāṃ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ //
1.13.d:
ध्रमिकौ रूपसंपन्नौ सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरौ ।
मत्प्रसादादसंदिग्धं पुत्रौ तव भविष्यतः ।
एकमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशः स्वकीयां प्रकृतिं गतः ॥
1.13.m: "Two righteous sons endowed with beauty, the best among all wielders of weapons, / shall undoubtedly be born to you by my grace." / Having spoken this, Hṛṣīkeśa returned to his own natural state.

1.13.s:
vainyo 'pi vedavidhinā niścalāṃ bhaktimudvahan /
apālayat svakaṃ rājyaṃ nyāyena madhusūdane //
1.13.d:
वैन्यो ऽपि वेदविधिना निश्चलां भक्तिमुद्वहन् ।
अपालयत् स्वकं राज्यं न्यायेन मधुसूदने ॥
1.13.m: Vainya too, maintaining unswerving devotion to Madhusūdana / in accordance with Vedic injunctions, ruled his kingdom with justice.

1.13.s:
acirādeva tanvaṅgo bhāryā tasya sucismitā /
khikhaṇḍanaṃ havirdhānamantardhānā vyajāyata //
1.13.d:
अचिरादेव तन्वङ्गो भार्या तस्य सुचिस्मिता ।
खिखण्डनं हविर्धानमन्तर्धाना व्यजायत ॥
1.13.m: Before long, his slender-bodied wife of sweet smiles, / Antardhānā, gave birth to Shikhaṇḍin and Havirdhāna.

1.13.s:
śikhaṇḍano 'bhavat putraḥ suśīla iti viśrutaḥ /
dhārmiko rūpasaṃpanno vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ //
1.13.d:
शिखण्डनो ऽभवत् पुत्रः सुशील इति विश्रुतः ।
धार्मिको रूपसंपन्नो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ॥
1.13.m: The son Shikhaṇḍin became renowned as Suśīla: / righteous, endowed with beauty, and a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

1.13.s:
so 'dhītya vidhivad vedān dharmeṇa tapasi sthitaḥ /
matiṃ cakre bhāgyayogāt saṃnyāṃ prati dharmavit //
1.13.d:
सो ऽधीत्य विधिवद् वेदान् धर्मेण तपसि स्थितः ।
मतिं चक्रे भाग्ययोगात् संन्यां प्रति धर्मवित् ॥
1.13.m: Having studied the Vedas according to rule, abiding in austerity through righteousness, / that knower of duty, through the fruition of good fortune, set his mind on renunciation.

1.13.s:
sa kṛtvā tīrthasaṃsevāṃ svādhyāye tapasi sthitaḥ /
jagāma himavatpṛṣṭhaṃ kadācit siddhasevitam //
1.13.d:
स कृत्वा तीर्थसंसेवां स्वाध्याये तपसि स्थितः ।
जगाम हिमवत्पृष्ठं कदाचित् सिद्धसेवितम् ॥
1.13.m: Having frequented sacred pilgrimage sites and remaining steadfast in study and austerity, / he once went to the back of the Himavat, frequented by Siddhas.

1.13.s:
tatra dharmapadaṃ nāma dharmasiddhipradaṃ vanam /
apaśyad yogināṃ gamyamagamyaṃ brahmavidviṣām //
1.13.d:
तत्र धर्मपदं नाम धर्मसिद्धिप्रदं वनम् ।
अपश्यद् योगिनां गम्यमगम्यं ब्रह्मविद्विषाम् ॥
1.13.m: There he saw a forest named Dharmapada, granting the perfection of duty, / accessible to yogins, but inaccessible to those who hate the Veda.

1.13.s:
tatra mandākinī nāma supuṇyā vimalā nadī /
padmotpalavanopetā siddhāśramavibhūṣitā //
1.13.d:
तत्र मन्दाकिनी नाम सुपुण्या विमला नदी ।
पद्मोत्पलवनोपेता सिद्धाश्रमविभूषिता ॥
1.13.m: There flowed the extremely holy, stainless river named Mandākinī, / filled with clusters of lotuses and water lilies, adorned with the hermitages of Siddhas.

1.13.s:
sa tasyā dakṣiṇe tīre munīndrairyogibhirvṛtam /
supuṇyamāśramaṃ ramyamapaśyat prītisaṃyutaḥ //
1.13.d:
स तस्या दक्षिणे तीरे मुनीन्द्रैर्योगिभिर्वृतम् ।
सुपुण्यमाश्रमं रम्यमपश्यत् प्रीतिसंयुतः ॥
1.13.m: On its southern bank, he, filled with joy, / saw a delightful, sacred hermitage surrounded by eminent sages and yogins.

1.13.s:
mandākinījale strātvā saṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ /
arcayitvā mahādevaṃ puṣpaiḥ padmotpalādibhiḥ //
1.13.d:
मन्दाकिनीजले स्त्रात्वा संतर्प्य पितृदेवताः ।
अर्चयित्वा महादेवं पुष्पैः पद्मोत्पलादिभिः ॥
1.13.m: Bathing in the water of the Mandākinī, offering libations to the ancestors and gods, / and worshipping Mahādeva with flowers such as lotuses and water lilies,

1.13.s:
dhyātvārkaṃsaṃsthamīśānaṃ śirasyādhāya cāñjalim /
saṃprekṣamāṇo bhāsvantaṃ tuṣṭāva parameśvaram //
1.13.d:
ध्यात्वार्कंसंस्थमीशानं शिरस्याधाय चाञ्जलिम् ।
संप्रेक्षमाणो भास्वन्तं तुष्टाव परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.13.m: meditating on Īśāna dwelling in the sun, placing his folded hands upon his head, / and gazing upon the radiant sun, he praised the Supreme Lord,

1.13.s:
rudrādhyāyena giriśaṃ rudrasya caritena ca /
anyaiśca vividhaiḥ stotraiḥ śāṃbhavairvedasaṃbhavaiḥ //
1.13.d:
रुद्राध्यायेन गिरिशं रुद्रस्य चरितेन च ।
अन्यैश्च विविधैः स्तोत्रैः शांभवैर्वेदसंभवैः ॥
1.13.m: the mountain-dweller, with the Rudrādhyāya, with the deeds of Rudra, / and with various other hymns sacred to Śiva, originating from the Vedas.

1.13.s:
athāsminnantare 'paśyat tamāyāntaṃ mahāmunim /
śvetāśvataranāmānaṃ mahāpāśupatottamam //
1.13.d:
अथास्मिन्नन्तरे ऽपश्यत् तमायान्तं महामुनिम् ।
श्वेताश्वतरनामानं महापाशुपतोत्तमम् ॥
1.13.m: Then, in the meantime, he saw arriving that great sage / named Śvetāśvatara, the foremost of the great Pāśupatas,

1.13.s:
bhasmasaṃdigdhasavāṅgaṃ kaupīnācchādanānvitam /
tapasā karṣitātmānaṃ śuklayajñopavītinam //
1.13.d:
भस्मसंदिग्धसवाङ्गं कौपीनाच्छादनान्वितम् ।
तपसा कर्षितात्मानं शुक्लयज्ञोपवीतिनम् ॥
1.13.m: his entire body smeared with ashes, wearing a loincloth as clothing, / his body emaciated by austerities, wearing a white sacred thread.

1.13.s:
samāpya saṃstavaṃ śaṃbhorānandāstrāvilekṣaṇaḥ /
vavande śirasā pādau prāñjalirvākyamabravīt //
1.13.d:
समाप्य संस्तवं शंभोरानन्दास्त्राविलेक्षणः ।
ववन्दे शिरसा पादौ प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
1.13.m: Concluding his hymn of praise to Śambhu, his eyes blurred with tears of joy, / he bowed his head at the sage's feet and, with palms joined, said:

1.13.s:
dhanyo 'smyanugṛhīto 'smi yanme sākṣānmunīśvaraḥ /
yogīśvaro 'dya bhagavān dṛṣṭo yogavidāṃ varaḥ //
1.13.d:
धन्यो ऽस्म्यनुगृहीतो ऽस्मि यन्मे साक्षान्मुनीश्वरः ।
योगीश्वरो ऽद्य भगवान् दृष्टो योगविदां वरः ॥
1.13.m: "I am blessed, I am graced, that in person the lord of sages, / the lord of yogins, the venerable one, the best among knowers of yoga, has been seen by me today.

1.13.s:
aho me sumahadbhāgyaṃ tapāṃsi saphalāni me /
kiṃ kariṣyāmi śiṣyo 'haṃ tava māṃ pālayānagha //
1.13.d:
अहो मे सुमहद्भाग्यं तपांसि सफलानि मे ।
किं करिष्यामि शिष्यो ऽहं तव मां पालयानघ ॥
1.13.m: Oh, how great is my fortune! My austerities have borne fruit! / What shall I do? I am your disciple; protect me, sinless one!"

1.13.s:
so 'nugṛhyātha rājānaṃ suśīlaṃ śīlasaṃyutam /
śiṣyatve parijagrāha tapasā kṣīṇakalpaṣam //
1.13.d:
सो ऽनुगृह्याथ राजानं सुशीलं शीलसंयुतम् ।
शिष्यत्वे परिजग्राह तपसा क्षीणकल्पषम् ॥
1.13.m: He, having thus shown grace to King Suśīla who was endowed with good conduct, / accepted as a disciple that king whose blemishes were destroyed by austerity.

1.13.s:
sāṃnyāsikaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ kārayitvā vicakṣaṇaḥ /
dadau tadaiśvaraṃ jñānaṃ svaśākhāvihitaṃ vratam //
1.13.d:
सांन्यासिकं विधिं कृत्स्नं कारयित्वा विचक्षणः ।
ददौ तदैश्वरं ज्ञानं स्वशाखाविहितं व्रतम् ॥
1.13.m: The wise sage, having caused him to perform the entire rite of renunciation, / imparted that divine knowledge and the observance prescribed for his own Vedic branch,

1.13.s:
aśeṣavedasāraṃ tat paśupāśavimocanam /
antyāśramamiti khyātaṃ brahmādibhiranuṣṭhitam //
1.13.d:
अशेषवेदसारं तत् पशुपाशविमोचनम् ।
अन्त्याश्रममिति ख्यातं ब्रह्मादिभिरनुष्ठितम् ॥
1.13.m: which is the essence of all the Vedas, which releases the individual soul from bondage, / known as the final stage of life, practiced by Brahmā and others.

1.13.s:
uvāca śiṣyān saṃprekṣya ye tadāśramavāsinaḥ /
brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān vaiśyān brahmacaryaparāyaṇān //
1.13.d:
उवाच शिष्यान् संप्रेक्ष्य ये तदाश्रमवासिनः ।
ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियान् वैश्यान् ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणान् ॥
1.13.m: Looking at the disciples who dwelt in that hermitage— / Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas devoted to celibate studentship—he said:

1.13.s:
mayā pravartitāṃ śākhāmadhītyaiveha yoginaḥ /
samāsate mahādevaṃ dhyāyanto niṣkalaṃ śivam //
1.13.d:
मया प्रवर्तितां शाखामधीत्यैवेह योगिनः ।
समासते महादेवं ध्यायन्तो निष्कलं शिवम् ॥
1.13.m: "Having studied the branch set forth by me right here, the yogins / remain absorbed in meditation on Mahādeva, the partless Śiva.

1.13.s:
iha devo mahādevo ramamāṇaḥ sahomayā /
adhyāste bhagavānīśo bhaktānāmanukampayā //
1.13.d:
इह देवो महादेवो रममाणः सहोमया ।
अध्यास्ते भगवानीशो भक्तानामनुकम्पया ॥
1.13.m: Here, the divine Mahādeva, sporting with Umā, / the blessed Lord, resides out of compassion for his devotees.

1.13.s:
ihāśeṣajagaddhātā purā nārāyaṇaḥ svayam /
ārādhayanmahādevaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
1.13.d:
इहाशेषजगद्धाता पुरा नारायणः स्वयम् ।
आराधयन्महादेवं लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
1.13.m: Here in ancient times Nārāyaṇa himself, the creator of the whole world, / worshipped Mahādeva out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.

1.13.s:
ihaiva devamīśānaṃ devānāmapi daivatam /
ārādhya mahatīṃ siddhiṃ lebhire devadānavāḥ //
1.13.d:
इहैव देवमीशानं देवानामपि दैवतम् ।
आराध्य महतीं सिद्धिं लेभिरे देवदानवाः ॥
1.13.m: Right here, having worshipped the god Īśāna, the deity even of the gods, / the gods and Dānavas attained great perfection.

1.13.s:
ihaiva munayaḥ pūrvaṃ marīcyādyā maheśvaram /
dṛṣṭvā tapobalājjñānaṃ lebhire sārvakālikam //
1.13.d:
इहैव मुनयः पूर्वं मरीच्याद्या महेश्वरम् ।
दृष्ट्वा तपोबलाज्ज्ञानं लेभिरे सार्वकालिकम् ॥
1.13.m: Right here in former times, the sages Marīci and others, / having beheld Maheśvara through the power of austerities, attained eternal knowledge.

1.13.s:
tasmāt tvamapi rājendra tapoyogasamanvitaḥ /
tiṣṭha nityaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ tataḥ siddhimavāpsyasi //
1.13.d:
तस्मात् त्वमपि राजेन्द्र तपोयोगसमन्वितः ।
तिष्ठ नित्यं मया सार्धं ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
1.13.m: Therefore, O best of kings, endowed with austerity and yoga, / dwell constantly with me; thence you will attain perfection."

1.13.s:
evamābhāṣya viprendro devaṃ dhyātvā pinākinam /
ācacakṣe mahāmantraṃ yathāvat svārthasiddhaye //
1.13.d:
एवमाभाष्य विप्रेन्द्रो देवं ध्यात्वा पिनाकिनम् ।
आचचक्षे महामन्त्रं यथावत् स्वार्थसिद्धये ॥
1.13.m: Having thus spoken, the eminent Brahmin, meditating upon the god who bears the Pināka, / duly taught the great mantra for the attainment of his goal,

1.13.s:
sarvapāpopaśamanaṃ vedasāraṃ vimuktidam /
agnirityādikaṃ puṇyamṛṣibhiḥ saṃpravartitam //
1.13.d:
सर्वपापोपशमनं वेदसारं विमुक्तिदम् ।
अग्निरित्यादिकं पुण्यमृषिभिः संप्रवर्तितम् ॥
1.13.m: which calms all sins, is the essence of the Vedas, bestows liberation, / beginning with 'Agni…', holy, and promulgated by the sages.

1.13.s:
so 'pi tadvacanād rājā suśīlaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ /
sākṣāt pāśupato bhūtvā vedābhyāsarato 'bhavat //
1.13.d:
सो ऽपि तद्वचनाद् राजा सुशीलः श्रद्धयान्वितः ।
साक्षात् पाशुपतो भूत्वा वेदाभ्यासरतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.13.m: He too, King Suśīla, upon his word, endowed with faith, / became a direct Pāśupata and devoted himself to the study of the Veda,

1.13.s:
bhasmoddhūlitasarvāṅgaḥ kandamūlaphalāśanaḥ /
śānto dānto jitakrodhaḥ saṃnyāsavidhimāśritaḥ //
1.13.d:
भस्मोद्धूलितसर्वाङ्गः कन्दमूलफलाशनः ।
शान्तो दान्तो जितक्रोधः संन्यासविधिमाश्रितः ॥
1.13.m: his entire body dusted with ashes, eating roots, bulbs, and fruits, / calm, self-restrained, his anger conquered, having taken refuge in the rite of renunciation.

1.13.s:
havirdhānastathāgneyyāṃ janayāmāsa satsutam /
prācīnabarhiṣaṃ nāmnā dhanurvedasya pāragam //
1.13.d:
हविर्धानस्तथाग्नेय्यां जनयामास सत्सुतम् ।
प्राचीनबर्हिषं नाम्ना धनुर्वेदस्य पारगम् ॥
1.13.m: Havirdhāna likewise begot upon Āgneyī a noble son / named Prācīnabarhis, who was a master of the science of archery.

1.13.s:
prācīnabarhirbhāgavān sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ /
samudratanayāyāṃ vai daśa putrānajījanat //
1.13.d:
प्राचीनबर्हिर्भागवान् सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः ।
समुद्रतनयायां वै दश पुत्रानजीजनत् ॥
1.13.m: The venerable Prācīnabarhis, foremost among all wielders of weapons, / begot ten sons upon the daughter of the ocean.

1.13.s:
pracetasaste vikhyātā rājānaḥ prathitaijasaḥ /
adhītavantaḥ svaṃ vedaṃ nārāyaṇaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.13.d:
प्रचेतसस्ते विख्याता राजानः प्रथितैजसः ।
अधीतवन्तः स्वं वेदं नारायणपरायणाः ॥
1.13.m: They became famous as the Pracetases, kings of well-known majesty, / who had studied their own Veda and were devoted to Nārāyaṇa.

1.13.s:
daśabhyastu pracetobhyo māriṣāyāṃ prajāpatiḥ /
dakṣo jajñe mahābhāgo yaḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ //
1.13.d:
दशभ्यस्तु प्रचेतोभ्यो मारिषायां प्रजापतिः ।
दक्षो जज्ञे महाभागो यः पूर्वं ब्रह्मणः सुतः ॥
1.13.m: From the ten Pracetases, the lord of creatures, / the illustrious Dakṣa, who was formerly the son of Brahmā, was born of Māriṣā.

1.13.s:
sa tu dakṣo maheśena rudreṇa saha dhīmatā /
kṛtvā vivādaṃ rudreṇa śaptaḥ prācetaso 'bhavat //
1.13.d:
स तु दक्षो महेशेन रुद्रेण सह धीमता ।
कृत्वा विवादं रुद्रेण शप्तः प्राचेतसो ऽभवत् ॥
1.13.m: That Dakṣa, however, having engaged in an argument with the wise / Maheśa, Rudra, was cursed by Rudra and became the son of the Pracetases.

1.13.s:
samāyāntaṃ mahādevo dakṣaṃ devyā gṛhaṃ haraḥ /
dṛṣṭvā yathocitāṃ pūjāṃ dakṣāya pradadau svayam //
1.13.d:
समायान्तं महादेवो दक्षं देव्या गृहं हरः ।
दृष्ट्वा यथोचितां पूजां दक्षाय प्रददौ स्वयम् ॥
1.13.m: When Dakṣa arrived at the house of the Goddess, Mahādeva Hara, / seeing him, personally offered him appropriate worship.

1.13.s:
tadā vai tamasāviṣṭaḥ so 'dikāṃ brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ /
pūjāmanarhāmanvicchan jagāma kupito gṛham //
1.13.d:
तदा वै तमसाविष्टः सो ऽदिकां ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।
पूजामनर्हामन्विच्छन् जगाम कुपितो गृहम् ॥
1.13.m: Then indeed, overcome with darkness, that son of Brahmā, / seeking excessive and undeserved honor, went home enraged.

1.13.s:
kadācit svagṛhaṃ prāptāṃ satīṃ dakṣaḥ sudurmanāḥ /
bhartrā saha vinindyaināṃ bhartsayāmasā vai ruṣā //
1.13.d:
कदाचित् स्वगृहं प्राप्तां सतीं दक्षः सुदुर्मनाः ।
भर्त्रा सह विनिन्द्यैनां भर्त्सयामसा वै रुषा ॥
1.13.m: Once, when Satī had come to his house, Dakṣa, very wicked of mind, / reviling her along with her husband, rebuked her in anger:

1.13.s:
anye jāmātaraḥ śreṣṭhā bhartustava pinākinaḥ /
tvamapyasatsutāsmākaṃ gṛhād gaccha yathāgatam //
1.13.d:
अन्ये जामातरः श्रेष्ठा भर्तुस्तव पिनाकिनः ।
त्वमप्यसत्सुतास्माकं गृहाद् गच्छ यथागतम् ॥
1.13.m: "My other sons-in-law are superior to your husband, the bearer of the Pināka; / you too are our unworthy daughter; go from this house the way you came!"

1.13.s:
tasya tadvākyamākarṇya sā devī śaṅkarapriyā /
vinindya pitaraṃ dakṣaṃ dadāhātmānamātmanā //
1.13.d:
तस्य तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य सा देवी शङ्करप्रिया ।
विनिन्द्य पितरं दक्षं ददाहात्मानमात्मना ॥
1.13.m: Hearing that speech of his, the goddess, beloved of Śaṅkara, / reviled her father Dakṣa and burned herself by her own power.

1.13.s:
praṇamya paśubhartāraṃ bhartāraṃ kṛttivāsasam /
himavadduhitā sābhūt tapasā tasya toṣitā //
1.13.d:
प्रणम्य पशुभर्तारं भर्तारं कृत्तिवाससम् ।
हिमवद्दुहिता साभूत् तपसा तस्य तोषिता ॥
1.13.m: Bowing to her husband, the lord of creatures, who wears animal skins, / she became the daughter of Himavat, pleasing him by her austerity.

1.13.s:
jñātvā tadbhāgavān rudraḥ prapannārtiharo haraḥ /
śaśāpa dakṣaṃ kupitaḥ samāgatyātha tadgṛham //
1.13.d:
ज्ञात्वा तद्भागवान् रुद्रः प्रपन्नार्तिहरो हरः ।
शशाप दक्षं कुपितः समागत्याथ तद्गृहम् ॥
1.13.m: Learning of that, the blessed Rudra Hara, who removes the distress of the surrendered, / went in wrath to his house and cursed Dakṣa:

1.13.s:
tyaktvā dehamimaṃ brahman kṣatriyāṇāṃ kulodbhavaḥ /
svasyāṃ sutāyāṃ mūḍhātmā putramutpādayiṣyasi //
1.13.d:
त्यक्त्वा देहमिमं ब्रह्मन् क्षत्रियाणां कुलोद्भवः ।
स्वस्यां सुतायां मूढात्मा पुत्रमुत्पादयिष्यसि ॥
1.13.m: "Having abandoned this body, O Brahmin, you will be born in the lineage of Kṣatriyas, / and, dull-witted, you shall generate offspring upon your own daughter!"

1.13.s:
evamuktvā mahādevo yayau kālāsaparvatam /
svāyaṃbhuvo 'pi kālena dakṣaḥ prācetaso 'bhavat //
1.13.d:
एवमुक्त्वा महादेवो ययौ कालासपर्वतम् ।
स्वायंभुवो ऽपि कालेन दक्षः प्राचेतसो ऽभवत् ॥
1.13.m: Having spoken thus, Mahādeva departed to Mount Kailāsa. / In the course of time, Dakṣa, born of the Self-born, became the son of the Pracetases.

1.13.s:
etad vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasya tu /
visargaṃ dakṣaparyantaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ pāpanāśanam //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭmāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.13.d:
एतद् वः कथितं सर्वं मनोः स्वायंभुवस्य तु ।
विसर्गं दक्षपर्यन्तं शृण्वतां पापनाशनम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्माहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे त्रयोदशो ऽध्यायः
1.13.m:
All this has been recounted to you concerning the Manu Svāyambhuva, / the secondary creation down to Dakṣa, destroying the sins of those who hear it.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.14.s:
naimiṣīyā ūcuḥ
devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca gandharvoragarakṣasām /
utpattiṃ vistarāt sūta brūhi vaivasvate 'ntare //
1.14.d:
नैमिषीया ऊचुः
देवानां दानवानां च गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् ।
उत्पत्तिं विस्तरात् सूत ब्रूहि वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे ॥
1.14.m: The dwellers of Naimiṣa forest said: / The origin of the gods, the Dānavas, the Gandharvas, serpents, and Rakṣasas, / explain in detail, O Sūta, during the cosmic era of Vaivasvata.

1.14.s:
sa śaptaḥ śaṃbhunā pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ prācetaso nṛpaḥ /
kimakārṣonmahābuddhe śrotumicchāma sāṃpratam //
1.14.d:
स शप्तः शंभुना पूर्वं दक्षः प्राचेतसो नृपः ।
किमकार्षोन्महाबुद्धे श्रोतुमिच्छाम सांप्रतम् ॥
1.14.m: Cursed formerly by Śambhu, what did that king Dakṣa, / the son of the Pracetases, do, O one of great intellect? We wish to hear that now.

1.14.s:
sūta uvāca
vakṣye nārāyaṇenoktaṃ pūrvakalpānuṣaṅgikam /
trikālabaddhaṃ pāpaghnaṃ prajāsargasya vistaram //
1.14.d:
सूत उवाच
वक्ष्ये नारायणेनोक्तं पूर्वकल्पानुषङ्गिकम् ।
त्रिकालबद्धं पापघ्नं प्रजासर्गस्य विस्तरम् ॥
1.14.m: Sūta said: / I shall declare the creation of subjects, destroying sins, connected with the past kalpa, / bound to the three divisions of time, as spoken by Nārāyaṇa in detail.

1.14.s:
sa śaptaḥ śaṃbhunā pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ prācetaso nṛpaḥ /
vinindya pūrvavaireṇa gaṅgādvare 'yajad bhavam //
1.14.d:
स शप्तः शंभुना पूर्वं दक्षः प्राचेतसो नृपः ।
विनिन्द्य पूर्ववैरेण गङ्गाद्वरे ऽयजद् भवम् ॥
1.14.m: Cursed formerly by Śambhu, that king Dakṣa, the son of the Pracetases, / reviling Bhava because of former hostility, sacrificed at Gaṅgādvāra.

1.14.s:
devāśca sarve bhāgārthamāhūtā viṣṇunā saha /
sahaiva munibhiḥ sarvairāgatā munipuṅgavāḥ //
1.14.d:
देवाश्च सर्वे भागार्थमाहूता विष्णुना सह ।
सहैव मुनिभिः सर्वैरागता मुनिपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.14.m: All the gods were invited for their share, along with Viṣṇu, / and together with all the sages, O foremost sages, they arrived.

1.14.s:
dṛṣṭvā devakulaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śaṅkareṇa vināgatam /
dadhīco nāma viprarṣiḥ prācetasamathābravīt //
1.14.d:
दृष्ट्वा देवकुलं कृत्स्नं शङ्करेण विनागतम् ।
दधीचो नाम विप्रर्षिः प्राचेतसमथाब्रवीत् ॥
1.14.m: Seeing the entire host of gods arrived without Śaṅkara, / a brahmin-sage named Dadhīca then spoke to the son of the Pracetases.

1.14.s:
dadhīca uvāca
brahmādayaḥ piśācāntā yasyājñānuvidhāyinaḥ /
sa devaḥ sāṃprataṃ rudro vidhinā kiṃ na pūjyate //
1.14.d:
दधीच उवाच
ब्रह्मादयः पिशाचान्ता यस्याज्ञानुविधायिनः ।
स देवः सांप्रतं रुद्रो विधिना किं न पूज्यते ॥
1.14.m: Dadhīca said: / He whose command is obeyed by all from Brahmā down to the Piśācas— / why is that god Rudra not worshipped properly now?

1.14.s:
dakṣa uvāca
sarveṣveva hi yajñeṣu na bhāgaḥ parikalpitaḥ /
na mantrā bhāryayā sārdhaṃ śaṅkarasyeti nejyate //
1.14.d:
दक्ष उवाच
सर्वेष्वेव हि यज्ञेषु न भागः परिकल्पितः ।
न मन्त्रा भार्यया सार्धं शङ्करस्येति नेज्यते ॥
1.14.m: Dakṣa said: / In all sacrifices indeed, no portion has been allotted [to him], / nor are there mantras for Śaṅkara together with his wife; therefore he is not worshipped.

1.14.s:
vihasya dakṣaṃ kupito vacaḥ prāha mahāmuniḥ /
śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ sarvajñānamayaḥ svayam //
1.14.d:
विहस्य दक्षं कुपितो वचः प्राह महामुनिः ।
शृण्वतां सर्वदेवानां सर्वज्ञानमयः स्वयम् ॥
1.14.m: Laughing at Dakṣa, the great sage, embodying all knowledge, / being enraged, spoke these words while all the gods were listening.

1.14.s:
dadhīca uvāca
yataḥ pravṛttirviśveṣāṃ yaścāsya parameśvaraḥ /
saṃpūjyate sarvayajñairviditvā kila śaṅkaraḥ //
1.14.d:
दधीच उवाच
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्विश्वेषां यश्चास्य परमेश्वरः ।
संपूज्यते सर्वयज्ञैर्विदित्वा किल शङ्करः ॥
1.14.m: Dadhīca said: / He from whom is the manifestation of all things, and who is the supreme lord of this [universe], / having known him, Śaṅkara is indeed worshipped in all sacrifices.

1.14.s:
na hyaṃ śaṅkaro rudraḥ saṃhartā tāmaso haraḥ /
nagnaḥ kapālī vikṛto viśvātmā nopapadyate //
1.14.d:
न ह्यं शङ्करो रुद्रः संहर्ता तामसो हरः ।
नग्नः कपाली विकृतो विश्वात्मा नोपपद्यते ॥
1.14.m: [Dakṣa said:] / This Śaṅkara is not [the supreme lord]; Rudra is the destroyer, full of darkness, Hara; / naked, carrying a skull, deformed—it is not fitting that he be the universal Self.

1.14.s:
īśvaro hi jagatstraṣṭā prabhurnārāyaṇaḥ svarāṭ /
sattvātmako 'sau bhagavānijyate sarvakarmasu //
1.14.d:
ईश्वरो हि जगत्स्त्रष्टा प्रभुर्नारायणः स्वराट् ।
सत्त्वात्मको ऽसौ भगवानिज्यते सर्वकर्मसु ॥
1.14.m: For Nārāyaṇa is the sovereign Lord, the creator of the world, the master; / that Lord, whose nature is sattva, is worshipped in all rites.

1.14.s:
dadhīca uvāca
kiṃ tvayā bhagavāneṣa sahastrāṃśurna dṛśyate /
sarvalokaikasaṃhartā kālātmā parameśvaraḥ //
1.14.d:
दधीच उवाच
किं त्वया भगवानेष सहस्त्रांशुर्न दृश्यते ।
सर्वलोकैकसंहर्ता कालात्मा परमेश्वरः ॥
1.14.m: Dadhīca said: / Do you not see this thousand-rayed Lord, / the sole destroyer of all worlds, the soul of time, the supreme lord?

1.14.s:
yaṃ gṛṇantīha vidvāṃso dhārmikā brahmavādinaḥ /
so 'yaṃ sākṣī tīvrarociḥ kālātmā śāṅkarītanuḥ //
1.14.d:
यं गृणन्तीह विद्वांसो धार्मिका ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
सो ऽयं साक्षी तीव्ररोचिः कालात्मा शाङ्करीतनुः ॥
1.14.m: Whom the wise, righteous knowers of Brahman praise here, / he is this witness of fierce radiance, the soul of time, the form of Śaṅkara.

1.14.s:
eṣa rudro mahādevaḥ kaparde ca ghṛṇī haraḥ /
ādityo bhagavān sūryo nīlagrīvo vilohitaḥ //
1.14.d:
एष रुद्रो महादेवः कपर्दे च घृणी हरः ।
आदित्यो भगवान् सूर्यो नीलग्रीवो विलोहितः ॥
1.14.m: This Rudra is Mahādeva, the compassionate Hara with matted hair, / the blessed Āditya, Sūrya, blue-necked, and deep-red.

1.14.s:
saṃstūyate sahastrāṃśuḥ sāmagādhvaryuhotṛbhiḥ /
paśyainaṃ viśvakarmāṇaṃ rudramūrti trayīmayam //
1.14.d:
संस्तूयते सहस्त्रांशुः सामगाध्वर्युहोतृभिः ।
पश्यैनं विश्वकर्माणं रुद्रमूर्ति त्रयीमयम् ॥
1.14.m: The thousand-rayed one is praised by Sāman-singers, Adhvaryus, and Hotṛs; / behold him, the maker of everything, the form of Rudra, composed of the three Vedas!

1.14.s:
dakṣa uvāca
ya ete dvādaśādityā āgatā yajñabhāginaḥ /
sarve sūryā iti jñeyā na hyānyo vidyate raviḥ //
1.14.d:
दक्ष उवाच
य एते द्वादशादित्या आगता यज्ञभागिनः ।
सर्वे सूर्या इति ज्ञेया न ह्यान्यो विद्यते रविः ॥
1.14.m: Dakṣa said: / These twelve Ādityas who have come to receive their share of the sacrifice, / they are all known as suns; indeed, there is no other sun.

1.14.s:
evamukte tu munayaḥ samāyātā didṛkṣavaḥ /
bāḍhamityabruvan vākyaṃ tasya sāhāyyakāriṇaḥ //
1.14.d:
एवमुक्ते तु मुनयः समायाता दिदृक्षवः ।
बाढमित्यब्रुवन् वाक्यं तस्य साहाय्यकारिणः ॥
1.14.m: When this was spoken, the sages who had arrived to watch, / giving him assistance, said the words: "Indeed!"

1.14.s:
tamasāviṣṭamanaso na paśyanti vṛṣadhvajam /
sahastraśo 'tha śataśo bhūya eva vinindyate //
1.14.d:
तमसाविष्टमनसो न पश्यन्ति वृषध्वजम् ।
सहस्त्रशो ऽथ शतशो भूय एव विनिन्द्यते ॥
1.14.m: Their minds overcome by darkness, they did not see the bull-bannered [god]; / hundreds and thousands of times he was reviled again.

1.14.s:
nindanto vaidikān mantrān sarvabhūtapatiṃ haram /
apūjayan dakṣavākyaṃ mohitā viṣṇumāyayā //
1.14.d:
निन्दन्तो वैदिकान् मन्त्रान् सर्वभूतपतिं हरम् ।
अपूजयन् दक्षवाक्यं मोहिता विष्णुमायया ॥
1.14.m: Reviling the Vedic mantras and Hara, the lord of all beings, / deluded by Viṣṇu's illusory creative power, they honoured Dakṣa's word.

1.14.s:
devāśca sarve bhāgārthamāgatā vāsavādayaḥ /
nāpaśyan devamīśānamṛte nārāyaṇaṃ harim //
1.14.d:
देवाश्च सर्वे भागार्थमागता वासवादयः ।
नापश्यन् देवमीशानमृते नारायणं हरिम् ॥
1.14.m: And all the gods who had come for their portion, beginning with Indra, / did not see the god, the sovereign Lord, except as Hari Nārāyaṇa.

1.14.s:
hiraṇyagarbho bhagavān brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ /
paśyatāmeva sarveṣāṃ kṣaṇādantaradhīyata //
1.14.d:
हिरण्यगर्भो भगवान् ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मविदां वरः ।
पश्यतामेव सर्वेषां क्षणादन्तरधीयत ॥
1.14.m: The blessed Hiraṇyagarbha, Brahmā, the foremost of the knowers of Brahman, / disappeared in an instant while all were watching.

1.14.s:
antarhite bhagavati dakṣo nārāyaṇaṃ harim /
rakṣakaṃ jagatāṃ devaṃ jagāma śaraṇaṃ svayam //
1.14.d:
अन्तर्हिते भगवति दक्षो नारायणं हरिम् ।
रक्षकं जगतां देवं जगाम शरणं स्वयम् ॥
1.14.m: When the Lord had disappeared, Dakṣa himself took refuge / in Hari Nārāyaṇa, the protector, the god of the worlds.

1.14.s:
pravartayāmāsa ca taṃ yajñaṃ dakṣo 'tha nirbhayaḥ /
rakṣate bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śaraṇāgatarakṣakaḥ //
1.14.d:
प्रवर्तयामास च तं यज्ञं दक्षो ऽथ निर्भयः ।
रक्षते भगवान् विष्णुः शरणागतरक्षकः ॥
1.14.m: And Dakṣa then proceeded with that sacrifice without fear: / "The blessed Viṣṇu, protector of those who seek refuge, protects [it]."

1.14.s:
punaḥ prāha ca taṃ dakṣaṃ dadhīco bhagavānṛṣiḥ /
saṃprekṣyarṣigaṇān devān sarvān vai brahmavidviṣaḥ //
1.14.d:
पुनः प्राह च तं दक्षं दधीचो भगवानृषिः ।
संप्रेक्ष्यर्षिगणान् देवान् सर्वान् वै ब्रह्मविद्विषः ॥
1.14.m: The blessed sage Dadhīca spoke again to that Dakṣa, / looking at the hosts of sages and all the gods who hated Brahman:

1.14.s:
apūjyapūjane caiva pūjyānāṃ cāpyapūjane /
naraḥ pāpamavāpnoti mahad vai nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.14.d:
अपूज्यपूजने चैव पूज्यानां चाप्यपूजने ।
नरः पापमवाप्नोति महद् वै नात्र संशयः ॥
1.14.m: "In worshipping the unworthy of worship, and in not worshipping those worthy of worship, / a person incurs great sin indeed; there is no doubt in this.

1.14.s:
asatāṃ pragraho yatra satāṃ caiva vimānanā /
daṇḍo devakṛtastatra sadyaḥ patati dāruṇaḥ //
1.14.d:
असतां प्रग्रहो यत्र सतां चैव विमानना ।
दण्डो देवकृतस्तत्र सद्यः पतति दारुणः ॥
1.14.m: Where there is acceptance of the wicked and disrespect towards the virtuous, / a terrible divine punishment falls immediately there."

1.14.s:
evamuktvā tu viprarṣiḥ śaśāpeśvaravidviṣaḥ /
samāgatān brāhmaṇāṃstān dakṣasāhāyyakāriṇaḥ //
1.14.d:
एवमुक्त्वा तु विप्रर्षिः शशापेश्वरविद्विषः ।
समागतान् ब्राह्मणांस्तान् दक्षसाहाय्यकारिणः ॥
1.14.m: Having spoken thus, the brahmin-sage cursed those haters of the Lord, / the brahmins who had assembled to assist Dakṣa:

1.14.s:
yasmād bahiṣkṛtā vedā bhavadbhiḥ parameśvaraḥ /
vinindito mahādevaḥ śaṅkaro lokavanditaḥ //
1.14.d:
यस्माद् बहिष्कृता वेदा भवद्भिः परमेश्वरः ।
विनिन्दितो महादेवः शङ्करो लोकवन्दितः ॥
1.14.m: "Because the Vedas have been discarded by you, and the supreme lord, / Mahādeva, Śaṅkara, praised by all the worlds, has been reviled,

1.14.s:
bhaviṣyadhvaṃ trayībāhyāḥ sarve 'pīśvaravidviṣaḥ /
nindanto hyaiśvaraṃ mārgaṃ kuśāstrāsaktamānasāḥ //
1.14.d:
भविष्यध्वं त्रयीबाह्याः सर्वे ऽपीश्वरविद्विषः ।
निन्दन्तो ह्यैश्वरं मार्गं कुशास्त्रासक्तमानसाः ॥
